front_matter.purpose:
## Purpose

This Policy & Procedure Manual sets out how **[AGENCY NAME]**, an Assisted Living Facility (ALF) licensed by the Florida Agency for Health Care Administration (AHCA) under Chapter 429, Part I, Florida Statutes, and rule chapter 59A-36, Florida Administrative Code, operates day to day. Depending on the facility's license, this may include one or more specialty licenses: Extended Congregate Care (ECC), Limited Nursing Services (LNS) and Limited Mental Health (LMH).

The manual is intended to:

- Turn state licensing requirements into written, workable procedures for admission, resident care, medication practices, staffing and training, food service, records, resident contracts, finances, emergency management and physical plant.
- Give staff, residents, families and surveyors a consistent, documented description of how **[AGENCY NAME]** meets its obligations.
- Support resident safety, dignity, choice and rights, including the Resident Bill of Rights.
- Provide the written policies that Florida rules require a facility to keep and make available at the licensee's physical address, such as DNRO, medication, grievance and elopement policies.

### Important: this manual must be customized

This is a template. Before use, **[AGENCY NAME]** must:

1. Replace every **[AGENCY NAME]** placeholder and other bracketed field (administrator, addresses, phone numbers, license number, licensed capacity, specialty licenses held) with facility-specific information.
2. Delete or adapt sections that do not apply to the facility's license type (for example, ECC, LNS or LMH sections if the facility does not hold those licenses).
3. Make sure each procedure reflects what the facility actually does. A policy the facility does not follow is a compliance risk.

### Adoption, maintenance and training

- **Adoption:** The manual is not in effect until it has been reviewed and formally adopted by the facility's governing body (owner, board of directors or equivalent). Record the adoption date and approval in the facility's records.
- **Keeping it current:** Statutes, rules, forms and agency contact information change. The governing body and administrator must review the manual at least annually and whenever a relevant law, rule, form or facility practice changes. Record the revision date and what changed.
- **Staff training:** All staff must be trained on this manual, and on the policies relevant to their duties, at hire and whenever policies are revised. Keep training documentation in staff records. This training supplements the training required by Rule 59A-36.011, F.A.C. It does not replace it.

This manual is an operational tool and is not legal advice. If it conflicts with a current statute or rule, the statute or rule controls. Consult the facility's legal counsel or AHCA when in doubt.

## How to Use This Manual

### Who should use it

- **Owners and governing body:** adopt, review and approve the manual and any revisions.
- **Administrator and managers:** keep the manual current, make sure practice matches policy, and use it for staff orientation and supervision.
- **All staff:** know the policies for their role, follow them, and report gaps or problems to the administrator.
- **Residents, families and surveyors:** the manual (or the relevant policies) may be shared or requested. Keep it readily available at the licensee's physical address.

### Getting started

1. **Customize.** Fill in every **[AGENCY NAME]** placeholder and bracketed field, and remove sections that do not apply to the facility's license type.
2. **Verify.** Check each cited statute, rule and form against the current official text and the current AHCA forms before relying on it. Rules are amended, and form editions change.
3. **Adopt.** Have the governing body approve the manual. Record the adoption date and the person who approved it.
4. **Train.** Train all staff on the manual, document attendance, and re-train when policies change.
5. **Implement.** Put the forms, logs, postings and records the manual calls for in place (for example, the Bill of Rights posting, complaint numbers and the license on display).
6. **Review.** Review at least annually and after any inspection finding, incident, or change in law or operations.

### Conventions in this manual

- Citations appear in the form used by the governing rule or statute (for example, Rule 59A-36.006, F.A.C., or s. 429.26, F.S.).
- Bracketed text such as **[AGENCY NAME]** marks information the facility must supply.
- Requirements are summarized for operational use. The full text of the cited rule or statute controls.
- Where a policy is tied to a rule, the rule cite is given so staff can look up the full requirement.
- Figures that change over time (for example, minimum wage and Optional State Supplementation rates) should be confirmed against the current official source before use.

### Keeping a revision record

Keep a revision log at the front of the manual showing the date, the section changed, the reason, who approved it, and the date staff were trained on the change.

## Regulatory Framework

**[AGENCY NAME]** operates under the Florida laws and rules listed below. This list is drawn from the citations compiled for this manual. It is not exhaustive. Always check the current official text, since laws and rules change.

### Governing statutes (Florida Statutes)

- **s. 429.07, F.S.**: License required; fee. A license is required to operate an ALF. Specialty licenses (ECC and LNS) are authorized, and license fees are biennial.
- **s. 429.075, F.S.**: Limited mental health license. License requirements and training for facilities serving mental health residents.
- **s. 429.174, F.S.**: Background screening. Level 2 screening of owners, administrators and staff.
- **s. 429.24, F.S.**: Contracts. Resident contract content and refund policy, implemented by Rule 59A-36.018, F.A.C.
- **s. 429.255, F.S.**: Use of personnel; emergency care. Facilities with 17 or more beds must keep a working automated external defibrillator (AED) on the premises. The section also underpins the DNRO rule.
- **s. 429.26, F.S.**: Appropriateness of placements; examinations of residents. Medical examination within 60 days before or 30 days after admission, hospice exceptions, and disagreements about placement appropriateness.
- **s. 429.27, F.S.**: Property and personal affairs of residents. Surety bond when the facility acts as representative payee or under a power of attorney, and safekeeping of resident funds and personal effects.
- **s. 429.275, F.S.**: Business practice; personnel records; liability insurance.
- **s. 429.28, F.S.**: Resident bill of rights. Includes grievance and facility-procedure rights. *Subsection details were not independently re-verified in preparing this manual. Confirm them against the current statute before quoting.*
- **s. 429.52, F.S.**: Staff training and educational requirements. Statutory basis for core training, administrator continuing education and medication-assistance training.
- **s. 408.809, F.S.**: Background screening; prohibited offenses. Level 2 screening standards, including rescreening every 5 years.
- **s. 435.12, F.S.**: Care Provider Background Screening Clearinghouse. Screening results are shared through the AHCA Clearinghouse (help line 850-412-4503).
- **s. 409.982, F.S.**: Long-term care managed care plan accountability. SMMC LTC plans and ALFs negotiate rates. There is no state rate table.
- **s. 409.212 and Rule 65A-2.036, F.A.C.**: Optional State Supplementation (OSS). The Department of Children and Families (DCF) determines eligibility. Confirm current OSS rates with DCF before use.

### Governing rules (Florida Administrative Code)

**Chapter 59A-36 (Assisted Living Facilities)**

- **Rule 59A-36.003, F.A.C.**: Licensing and Change of Ownership.
- **Rule 59A-36.004, F.A.C.**: License Requirements. This includes limits on representing services beyond the license, capacity changes, use of uninspected space, contiguous property, and submitting annual fire and sanitation inspection copies to AHCA.
- **Rule 59A-36.005, F.A.C.**: Inspection Responsibilities. The county health department inspects sanitation, food hygiene and biomedical waste. The local fire authority or State Fire Marshal inspects fire safety. AHCA inspects everything else.
- **Rule 59A-36.006, F.A.C.**: Admission Procedures, Appropriateness of Placement and Continued Residency Criteria.
- **Rule 59A-36.007, F.A.C.**: Resident Care Standards. This includes supervision, activities, the Bill of Rights posting, grievance procedure, elopement, restraints, assistive devices and infection control.
- **Rule 59A-36.008, F.A.C.**: Medication Practices.
- **Rule 59A-36.009, F.A.C.**: Do Not Resuscitate Orders (DNROs).
- **Rule 59A-36.010, F.A.C.**: Staffing Standards.
- **Rule 59A-36.011, F.A.C.**: Staff Training Requirements and Competency Test.
- **Rule 59A-36.012, F.A.C.**: Food Service Standards.
- **Rule 59A-36.013, F.A.C.**: Fiscal Standards. This includes resident trust funds, surety bond and liability insurance.
- **Rule 59A-36.014, F.A.C.**: Physical Plant Standards.
- **Rule 59A-36.015, F.A.C.**: Records.
- **Rule 59A-36.018, F.A.C.**: Resident Contracts.
- **Rule 59A-36.019, F.A.C.**: Emergency Management.
- **Rule 59A-36.020, F.A.C.**: Limited Mental Health.
- **Rule 59A-36.021, F.A.C.**: Extended Congregate Care Services.
- **Rule 59A-36.022, F.A.C.**: Limited Nursing Services.
- **Rule 59A-36.025, F.A.C.**: Emergency Environmental Control for Assisted Living Facilities.

**Other rules and provisions**

- **Rule 59A-35.060, F.A.C.**: Health care licensing application procedures. This includes online licensing and renewal filing.
- **Fla. Const. Art. X, s. 24**: Florida minimum wage, which applies to staff compensation. Confirm the current rate before setting wages.

*Specialty license sections of this manual (ECC, LNS, LMH) apply only if **[AGENCY NAME]** holds the corresponding license.*

### Regulators and contacts

Contact details below are those on file. Confirm them before publishing the manual, and add facility-specific contacts (such as the local county health department, fire authority and emergency management office) where marked.

### Keeping the framework current

This section reflects the sources compiled for this manual. **[AGENCY NAME]** must monitor changes to Chapter 429 and Chapter 408, F.S., rule chapter 59A-36, F.A.C., and AHCA forms. It must update this section and the affected policies when changes occur, have the governing body adopt the revisions, and train staff on them.

citations.title: License Requirements
citations.requirement: Facility may not represent any service beyond its license (1). Capacity changes need prior AHCA Central Office approval (2). Converting uninspected space to resident use needs prior Field Office approval (3). Buildings under one license must be on contiguous property (4). Copies of annual fire and sanitation inspections go to AHCA Central Office within 30 calendar days (5). Facility must identify state-funded residents on request (6).

citations.title: Admission Procedures, Appropriateness of Placement and Continued Residency Criteria
citations.requirement: (1) Admission criteria, including age 18+, no stage 3-4 pressure sores, not bedridden except hospice, and the listed nursing services that exclude a resident. (2) Face-to-face medical exam within 60 days before or 30 days after admission, on AHCA Form 1823 or the practitioner's form. (3) Admission package contents, and what the resident receives at or before admission. (4) Continued residency: exam at least every 3 years or after a significant change, bedridden limit of 7 consecutive days, stage 2 sore conditions, and terminally ill/hospice retention.

citations.title: Resident Care Standards
citations.requirement: (1) Supervision and written record of significant changes. (2) Activities program (12 hrs/week, 6 days/week). (3) Arrangement for health care and transportation. (5) Bill of Rights posting, written grievance procedure, posted complaint numbers in 14-point type, house rules, no uncompensated work, telephone access. (6) Third-party services and 30-day communication. (7) Elopement standards. (8) Physical restraint care plan. (9) Assistive devices. (10) Infection control: hand hygiene, standard precautions, equipment disinfection.

citations.title: Medication Practices
citations.requirement: Rules for self-administration, pill organizers, assistance with self-administration by trained unlicensed staff, and administration by licensed staff. Also CLIA certificate when facility staff perform lab tests, medication observation records, storage (locked, central storage triggers), disposal timelines, labeling and orders, and OTC/stock supply.

citations.title: Do Not Resuscitate Orders (DNROs)
citations.requirement: Written DNRO policies. A DNRO may not be required as a condition of admission. At admission, give Form SCHS-4-2006 (or equivalent) and DH Form 1896. Document in the record whether DH Form 1896 is executed. Honor an executed form. Hospice procedures take precedence in an arrest.

citations.title: Staffing Standards
citations.requirement: (1) Administrator qualifications (21+, HS/GED, Level 2 screening, core training and competency test within 90 days), up to 3 facilities, managers appointed in writing, and notice of administrator change within 10 days on AHCA Form 3180-1006. (2) Staff health statement within 30 days, annual TB documentation, Level 2 for staff and contracted staff, written contracts with staffing agencies. (3) Minimum weekly staff-hours table, awake overnight staff at 17+ residents, CPR/First Aid staff at all times, in-charge rules during administrator absence, written 24-hour schedule, AHCA authority to order more staff.

citations.title: Staff Training Requirements and Competency Test
citations.requirement: 26-hr core training plus competency test (75% to pass) within 3 months; 12 hrs CE every 2 years. 2-hr preservice orientation before resident contact. In-service training: infection control, adverse incidents and emergency procedures, resident rights and abuse, behavior and ADLs, safe food handling, elopement, HIV/AIDS. First Aid/CPR. 6-hr medication-assistance course with 2 hrs annual CE. Food service CE. ECC, LMH and ADRD training.

citations.title: Food Service Standards
citations.requirement: Written food service designee. USDA Dietary Guidelines-based menus, reviewed annually by a dietitian or nutritionist. Menus planned 1 week ahead, and menus as served kept 6 months. Therapeutic diets as ordered. Meal-interval limits. 3-day nonperishable food supply. County health department reports kept for 2 years. Contracted food service documentation.

citations.title: Fiscal Standards
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: resident trust funds not co-mingled with facility funds (a single trust account is allowed with separate written accounting per resident) (2). Surety bond if the facility is representative payee or holds power of attorney (3). Liability insurance in force at all times, with proof filed at each renewal or policy change (4).

citations.title: Records
citations.requirement: Records must be readily available at the licensee's physical address. Lists required facility records, including the admission/discharge log, required policies, inspection reports, and the license on display. Also required staff records, resident records, retention (resident contracts 5 years; other resident records 2 years after departure), and inspection access.

citations.title: Resident Contracts
citations.requirement: Contract offered before or at admission with required provisions: services and rates, 30-day written notice of rate increases, deposits and refund policy, written bed hold policy, religious affiliation, transfer notice, 3-year assessment, medication and DNRO policies. Resident gets a copy. Additional charges need an itemized statement and a signed, dated addendum.

citations.title: Emergency Management
citations.requirement: Written CEMP on AHCA Form 3180-5006 (Sept 2023) covering the listed components. Annual submission and county emergency management approval, with significant modifications submitted within 30 days. Staff trained within 30 days of hire. Evacuation reporting within 6 hours. Emergency shelter above licensed capacity with a 48-hour report and a log.

citations.title: Emergency Environmental Control for Assisted Living Facilities
citations.requirement: Plan to hold ambient temperature at or below 81°F for 96 hours after power loss. At least 20 net sq ft per resident, calculated on 80% of licensed beds. Fuel onsite: 48 hrs (16 or fewer beds) or 72 hrs (17+). Carbon monoxide alarm. Plan submitted before licensure. Proof of county approval sent to AHCA within 30 days. Written heat-injury mitigation procedures. Notice to residents within 5 business days.

citations.title: Inspection Responsibilities
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: county health department inspects sanitation, food hygiene and biomedical waste (1). Local fire authority or State Fire Marshal inspects fire safety (2). AHCA inspects everything else (3).

citations.title: Physical Plant Standards
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: Florida Building Code and ch. 69A-40 fire standards (1)-(2). Resident furnishings (3): bed with mattress at least 36x72 inches, closet or wardrobe, dresser, nightstand or table, lamp, wastebasket. Facility keeps master keys, and provides linens and laundry service.

citations.title: Limited Mental Health
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: LMH facility requirements, including a community living support plan and cooperative agreement per mental health resident. Records requirements cross-referenced in 59A-36.015(3)(r). Staffing cross-referenced in 59A-36.010(3)(f).

citations.title: Extended Congregate Care Services
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: ECC license requirements, including a nurse on staff or under contract, monthly nursing assessments, quarterly service plan review, adequate awake staff at all hours, and ECC admission/residency criteria and disclosure.

citations.title: Limited Nursing Services
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: LNS facility must employ or contract a nurse available as needed. Services require a practitioner's order. Monthly nursing assessments and nursing progress notes are kept.

citations.title: Licensing and Change of Ownership
citations.requirement: Licensure application and change-of-ownership procedures (per fact-checked research).

citations.title: License required; fee
citations.requirement: A license is required to operate an ALF (subsec. 1). Specialty licenses ECC and LNS (subsec. 3). Biennial fees (subsec. 4).

citations.title: Limited mental health license
citations.requirement: LMH license requirements and training for facilities serving mental health residents.

citations.title: Contracts
citations.requirement: Resident contract content and refund policy; implemented by Rule 59A-36.018.

citations.title: Appropriateness of placements; examinations of residents
citations.requirement: Medical examination within 60 days before or 30 days after admission (subsec. 5). Hospice exceptions (subsec. 1). Disagreement on placement appropriateness (subsec. 8), as referenced in Rules 59A-36.006 and 59A-36.018.

citations.title: Use of personnel; emergency care
citations.requirement: Facilities with 17 or more beds must keep a working AED on the premises (subsec. 3(a)). The section also underpins the DNRO rule.

citations.title: Property and personal affairs of residents
citations.requirement: Surety bond when acting as representative payee or under a power of attorney (subsec. 2). Safekeeping of up to $500 cash and $500 in personal effects by mutual consent, and verified statements at least every 3 months (subsecs. 3-4), per fact-checked research.

citations.title: Business practice; personnel records; liability insurance
citations.requirement: Records, personnel records and liability insurance (subsec. 3) requirements, per fact-checked research.

citations.title: Resident bill of rights
citations.requirement: Resident Bill of Rights, grievance and facility-procedure rights. It is cited in Rules 59A-36.007(5) and 59A-36.011 and in the fact-checked research. Section text was not independently re-fetched in this pass, so confirm subsection details before quoting them.

citations.title: Staff training and educational requirements
citations.requirement: Statutory basis for core training, 12-hour administrator CE (subsec. 5) and the medication-assistance training (subsec. 6).

citations.title: Background screening
citations.requirement: Level 2 background screening of owners, administrators and staff.

citations.title: Background screening; prohibited offenses
citations.requirement: Level 2 screening standards, with rescreening every 5 years (subsec. 2), per fact-checked research.

citations.title: Care Provider Background Screening Clearinghouse
citations.requirement: Screening results are shared through the AHCA Clearinghouse (help line 850-412-4503 per fact-checked research).

citations.title: Long-term care managed care plan accountability
citations.requirement: SMMC LTC plans and ALFs negotiate rates. There is no state rate table.

citations.title: Health care licensing application procedures
citations.requirement: Online licensing and renewal filing. Per fact-checked research, renewals must be filed online (effective 3/5/2024).

citations.title: Florida minimum wage
citations.requirement: Minimum wage is $15.00/hr from Sept 30, 2026.

citations.title: Optional State Supplementation
citations.requirement: OSS base provider rate $991.40/month and $160 personal needs allowance (eff. 6/24/2025), per fact-checked research. DCF determines eligibility.

policies.title: Organization, Governing Body and Administrator Responsibilities
policies.applies_to: Licensee/owner, governing body, administrator, managers and all department leads of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To establish who governs [AGENCY NAME], who is accountable for daily operation, and how administrator and manager appointments, qualifications and changes are made and reported to the Florida Agency for Health Care Administration (AHCA).
policies.policy: The licensee (governing body) names the administrator and is responsible for providing the administrator with the authority and resources to run the facility. The administrator is responsible for operation and maintenance of the facility, management of all staff, and appropriate care of all residents under Chapter 408, Part II, and Chapter 429, Part I, Florida Statutes, and rule chapters 59A-35 and 59A-36, F.A.C. (Rule 59A-36.010(1)). The administrator must meet the qualifications in Rule 59A-36.010(1): at least 21 years of age, a high school diploma or GED, Level 2 background screening, and completion of the core training program and competency test within 90 days. The administrator may supervise a maximum of 3 facilities or a single-campus group. A written manager appointment is required for each facility. For up to 3 facilities of 16 or fewer beds each within 15 miles of one another, only 2 managers are required. A manager must meet the administrator qualifications and may not manage more than one facility, except as just described. The owner notifies AHCA Central Office within 10 days of any change of administrator on AHCA Form 3180-1006. The administrator monitors the continued appropriateness of each resident's placement at all times. Any change of ownership follows the licensure and change-of-ownership procedures in Rule 59A-36.003.

definitions.definition: The person or entity to which AHCA issues the assisted living facility license and that holds ultimate legal responsibility for the facility.
The owner(s), board or other persons who act for the licensee and appoint the administrator.
The individual designated by the licensee who is responsible for operation and maintenance of the facility, management of all staff, and appropriate care of residents.
An individual appointed in writing to manage a facility on behalf of an administrator who supervises more than one facility, who meets the administrator qualifications.
A transfer of the operation of the facility to a new licensee that requires licensure action with AHCA under Rule 59A-36.003.

procedures: The governing body adopts a written organizational chart showing the licensee, administrator, any managers, nurse/LNS staff (if applicable), and department leads, and reviews it at least annually.

Before appointing an administrator, the governing body verifies in writing that the candidate is at least 21 years old, holds a high school diploma or GED, and has a Level 2 background screening with no disqualifying offense (see STF-03).

The governing body confirms that the administrator has completed the core training program and passed the competency test (75% passing score) within 90 days of appointment, and records the certificate and score in the personnel file (see STF-06).
The governing body signs a written designation of the administrator that states the administrator's authority over operations, staff, admissions and discharges, and resident care.
The administrator tracks continuing education (12 hours every 2 years) with a calendar reminder and keeps the completion certificates on file.

When a person other than the administrator will manage a facility, the administrator issues a written manager appointment before the manager begins. The appointment names the facility and the effective date. A copy is placed in the personnel file and kept at the facility.

Before appointing a manager, the administrator verifies that the manager meets all administrator qualifications and does not manage another facility. The only exception is the 2-manager arrangement for up to 3 facilities of 16 or fewer beds each within 15 miles.

If one person will supervise more than one facility, the governing body confirms that the total does not exceed 3 facilities (or a single-campus group) and records the facilities covered in the written appointment.
When an administrator is replaced, the owner submits AHCA Form 3180-1006 to AHCA Central Office within 10 days of the change. The owner keeps the submission confirmation in the facility records.

Before any proposed sale, transfer or restructuring that may be a change of ownership, the governing body consults the Rule 59A-36.003 procedures and contacts the AHCA Assisted Living Unit at (850) 412-4304 or assistedliving@ahca.myflorida.com to confirm required filings. The facility does not operate under a new owner until AHCA approval is in place.

The administrator reviews each resident's continued appropriateness for placement at least whenever there is a change of condition and at each scheduled reassessment, and documents the review (see ADM-02 and ADM-04).

The administrator meets with the governing body at least quarterly to report on census, staffing, incidents, grievances, survey findings, budget, and QA results (see GOV-04), and the meeting is minuted.
The administrator ensures that staff know who is in charge at all times, and that absence coverage follows STF-02.
The governing body evaluates the administrator's performance annually and documents the evaluation.

responsibilities.duty: Appoints the administrator, provides resources, files administrator-change and ownership-change notices, and reviews quarterly administrator reports.
Operates the facility, manages staff, monitors resident placement appropriateness, maintains qualifications and continuing education, and appoints managers in writing.
Manages the assigned facility under the administrator's written appointment and meets all administrator qualifications.
Files appointments, training certificates, Form 3180-1006 confirmations and governing body minutes.

documentation: Organizational chart with annual review date
Written administrator designation and manager appointments
Administrator qualification file: age and education verification, Level 2 screening result, core training certificate and competency test score, continuing education certificates
AHCA Form 3180-1006 and proof of submission
Change-of-ownership filings and AHCA correspondence
Governing body meeting minutes and administrator performance evaluation

policies.title: Licensure, Posting and Regulatory Compliance
policies.applies_to: Licensee, administrator, managers and staff who handle regulatory filings, inspections and surveys
policies.purpose: To ensure [AGENCY NAME] is properly licensed, displays and keeps required licensure documents, stays within the scope of its license, files required reports on time, and is ready for AHCA, county health department and fire inspections.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] does not operate until AHCA issues the license (s. 429.07(1), F.S.). The license is displayed in a conspicuous public place (Rule 59A-36.015(1)(a)). The facility does not represent that it provides any service beyond what its license allows (Rule 59A-36.004(1)). Any change in licensed capacity requires prior approval from AHCA Central Office, and converting uninspected space to resident use requires prior approval from the AHCA Field Office (Rule 59A-36.004(2)-(3)). Buildings under one license must be on contiguous property (Rule 59A-36.004(4)). The facility holds only the licenses it has been issued (standard, and any of Extended Congregate Care (ECC), Limited Nursing Services (LNS) or Limited Mental Health (LMH)), and keeps admissions and services within that scope. The county health department inspects sanitation, food hygiene and biomedical waste. The local fire authority or State Fire Marshal inspects fire safety. AHCA inspects all other matters (Rule 59A-36.005). The facility sends copies of annual fire and sanitation inspection reports to AHCA Central Office within 30 calendar days of each inspection (Rule 59A-36.004(5)). Licenses are biennial, and renewal applications are filed online (Rule 59A-35.060; effective March 5, 2024). The facility identifies its state-funded residents to AHCA on request (Rule 59A-36.004(6)). Change-of-ownership and initial licensure procedures follow Rule 59A-36.003.

definitions.definition: The Florida Agency for Health Care Administration, which licenses and surveys assisted living facilities.
The base assisted living facility license under Chapter 429, Part I, Florida Statutes.
An additional license held by an ALF: Extended Congregate Care (ECC), Limited Nursing Services (LNS) or Limited Mental Health (LMH).
The number of residents the facility is licensed to serve, which may not be changed without prior AHCA approval.
An inspection by AHCA, including licensure, complaint and follow-up surveys.

procedures: Upon issuance, the administrator posts the original license in a conspicuous public location (such as the main lobby) where residents and visitors can see it, and verifies monthly that it is still displayed.

The administrator keeps a licensure tracking log listing the license number, license type, each specialty license held (ECC, LNS, LMH), licensed capacity, effective and expiration dates, and the date renewal is due.

The administrator checks all marketing materials, websites, admission agreements and verbal scripts before use to confirm that they describe only services the facility's license allows, and removes or corrects any that go beyond it.

Admission staff check the license log before accepting any resident who needs a specialty-licensed service (see ADM-01 and ADM-04). A resident needing a service the facility is not licensed for is not admitted, or is referred for discharge planning if already admitted.
Before any plan to change licensed capacity, the administrator submits a request to AHCA Central Office and waits for written approval before admitting beyond the current capacity.

Before any building area that has not been inspected is converted to resident use, the administrator requests approval from the AHCA Field Office and waits for written approval before resident use begins.

The administrator places the renewal date on the calendar and files the biennial renewal online through AHCA's system, targeting at least 60 days before expiration to avoid a late fee. A printout or confirmation of the submission is kept on file.

The administrator schedules the annual county health department sanitation inspection and the annual fire safety inspection with the local fire authority or State Fire Marshal, and records the date each inspection occurs.
Within 30 calendar days of each annual fire and sanitation inspection, the administrator sends copies of the reports to AHCA Central Office and documents the date and method of sending.

The administrator files in a binder or electronic folder at the facility address: AHCA survey, inspection and complaint reports and notices of sanctions for the last 5 years, and fire and sanitation inspection reports for the last 2 years. These are made available to residents and the public on request.

During any survey or inspection, the administrator (or the person in charge) greets inspectors, provides immediate access to the facility, records and staff, and keeps a log of records requested and delivered.

Within the deadline stated on any statement of deficiencies, the administrator submits a plan of correction. The administrator tracks each correction through completion and reports to the governing body and the QA review (see GOV-04).
On request, the administrator identifies to AHCA which residents are state-funded.

Staff direct all media or public inquiries about licensure status to the administrator. The AHCA Assisted Living Unit may be reached at (850) 412-4304 or assistedliving@ahca.myflorida.com for licensure questions.

responsibilities.duty: Maintains licensure, posts the license, files renewals, capacity and conversion requests and inspection reports, and manages surveys.
Approves capacity, conversion and ownership changes and funds timely renewal.
Confirms before each admission that needed services are within the facility's license.
Supports fire and sanitation inspections and corrects cited items.

documentation: Posted license and licensure tracking log
Online renewal confirmation
AHCA capacity and space-conversion approvals
Fire and sanitation inspection reports and proof of transmittal to AHCA Central Office (within 30 calendar days)
AHCA survey, inspection, complaint reports and sanction notices (5 years)
Fire and sanitation reports (2 years)
Plans of correction and corrective action tracking

policies.title: Policy Review and Document Control
policies.applies_to: Administrator, managers, and all staff who use or maintain the Policy & Procedure Manual and required facility records
policies.purpose: To ensure the written policies the state requires are adopted, kept current, readily available at the facility, and produced immediately on request to surveyors, residents and their representatives.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains a controlled Policy & Procedure Manual. Rule 59A-36.015(1) requires that the following written policies be on file and readily available at the licensee's address: the grievance procedure; elopement response; infection control; abuse prevention; medication practices; physical restraints; assistive devices; third-party providers; visitation; the do not resuscitate order (DNRO) policy; and the emergency power policies. Records may be kept electronically, but staff must be able to produce them immediately on request. The emergency power policies are also available for inspection by residents, their representatives and estates. Each policy is reviewed on a defined annual cycle, and the Comprehensive Emergency Management Plan (CEMP) is reviewed at least annually. Residents' rights under s. 429.27, F.S., including protection of resident property and personal affairs, are reflected in the facility's policies and may not be waived through document changes.

definitions.definition: A policy, procedure or form with a version number, effective date and approval signature that is tracked and distributed under this policy.
The written policies listed in Rule 59A-36.015(1) that must be on file and readily available at the licensee's address.
Able to be produced immediately on request at the facility's physical address, in paper or electronic form.

procedures: The administrator keeps a master index of all policies listing the policy ID, title, version, effective date, last review date and next review date.

The administrator maintains an up-to-date copy of the manual at the facility's physical address, in a binder at the administrator's office or the front desk, or as electronic files on a computer on site that any staff member on duty can open.

The administrator identifies on the master index each policy required by Rule 59A-36.015(1) and marks it as a required policy: grievance (RR-02), elopement (SAF-03), infection control (SAF-08), abuse prevention (SAF-01), medication practices (HCS-01 and HCS-02), physical restraints (SAF-04), assistive devices (HCS-10), third-party providers (HCS-08), visitation (SAF-09), DNRO (RR-06), and emergency power (SAF-06).

Each policy is reviewed at least once every 12 months by the administrator and the relevant department lead. The review is recorded on the policy review log with the reviewer's name, date and changes made, or a statement that no change was needed.
The CEMP (SAF-05) is reviewed at least annually, and the review is recorded on the same log.
The administrator also reviews affected policies within 30 days after any change in Florida law or rule, a survey finding, a serious incident, or a change in the services the facility offers.

Revisions are drafted with a new version number and effective date and approved by the administrator in writing before use. The governing body approves changes that alter services, fees or resident rights.
On the effective date, the administrator replaces the old version in the manual and removes obsolete copies from working areas. One superseded copy is archived and marked "superseded" with the date.
The administrator trains staff on every material change before the effective date, and staff sign the training roster (see STF-04).
If records are electronic, the administrator verifies at least quarterly that a staff member can open the required policies and produce a printed copy immediately, and keeps a backup copy.

When a surveyor, resident, resident representative or estate representative asks to see a required policy (including emergency power policies), staff provide it immediately, or notify the administrator, who provides it the same day. The request and the date given are logged.
The administrator keeps the resident-facing policies (for example, rights, grievance procedure and house rules) posted or available to residents, as described in RR-01 and RR-02.
Archived versions are kept for at least 5 years.

responsibilities.duty: Owns the manual and master index, schedules and records annual reviews, approves revisions and ensures availability at the facility.
Review and propose changes to the policies in their area and train staff on revisions.
Approves policy changes that affect services, fees or resident rights.
Know where policies are kept, follow current versions, and produce them on request.

documentation: Master policy index with version control
Policy review log with reviewer, date and outcome
Superseded policy archive
Staff training rosters on policy changes
Log of policy requests from surveyors, residents or their representatives
Electronic access and backup verification record

policies.title: Quality Assurance and Performance Improvement
policies.applies_to: Administrator, managers, department leads and the governing body of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To give [AGENCY NAME] a structured way to collect and review information about resident care and safety, identify problems early, and track corrective action to completion.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] operates a quality assurance and performance improvement (QAPI) program as an operator-level program tied to the administrator's responsibility for operation of the facility and care of all residents (Rule 59A-36.010(1)). The standard-license rules do not prescribe a specific QAPI committee, so this program is designed by the facility. The program reviews at least: grievances and resident suggestions (Rule 59A-36.007(5)); incident and accident reports; elopement drills; medication errors and discrepancies recorded on the medication observation record; infection control events; and findings from AHCA surveys. Any AHCA-ordered corrective action plan for increased staffing, and its modification or closure, is documented (Rule 59A-36.010(3)(d)).

definitions.definition: Quality assurance and performance improvement: the ongoing process of measuring care and safety and acting to improve them.
A written plan with assigned responsibility and due dates to fix a problem found through review, survey or AHCA order.
The record of medication assistance or administration for each resident, on which errors and omissions are documented.

procedures: The administrator appoints a QA team of at least the administrator, the lead for resident care (nurse or senior care staff), the dietary lead and the maintenance lead, and records the appointment.
The QA team meets at least quarterly. Minutes record attendees, data reviewed, findings and actions.

Before each meeting, the administrator compiles a data packet that includes: the grievance log and resident suggestions, the incident and accident log, medication error and omission counts from the medication observation records, elopement drill results, falls, skin injury and infection counts, and any AHCA, county health or fire inspection findings.
The team looks for trends by resident, by shift, by location and by staff member, and for any event that suggests a systemic cause.

For each problem found, the team writes a corrective action plan naming the person responsible, the action to take and a due date no later than 30 days out unless a longer date is justified in the minutes.
The administrator follows up on each open action at the next meeting and closes it only with documented evidence (for example, a training roster, repaired equipment or a re-audit).
Medication errors are reviewed for cause, and the team decides whether retraining, a change in the process or a pharmacy consultation is needed (see HCS-01 and HCS-02).
Grievances and suggestions received under RR-02 are reviewed for themes. The team confirms that each grievance was answered and resolved as the grievance procedure requires.
Elopement drill results are reviewed, and any delay in finding or accounting for residents leads to retraining and a repeat drill (see SAF-03).

If AHCA orders increased staffing through a corrective action plan, the administrator documents the order, the actions taken and the date of any request to modify or close the plan, and the QA team reviews progress at each meeting (see STF-01).
After any AHCA survey with findings, the QA team reviews each citation and its plan of correction and tracks completion (see GOV-02).
The administrator reports QA results to the governing body at least quarterly (see GOV-01).
Resident and family confidentiality is maintained in all QA materials. Resident identifiers are used only as needed (see RR-07).
QA minutes, data packets and corrective action plans are kept for at least 5 years.

responsibilities.duty: Leads the QA team, assembles data, assigns corrective actions, and reports to the governing body.
Review data for their areas, propose and complete corrective actions.
Reviews QA reports and provides resources for corrective action.
Report incidents, errors and concerns promptly and participate in corrective actions.

documentation: QA team appointment record
Quarterly QA meeting minutes and data packets
Corrective action plans with owners, due dates and closure evidence
AHCA-ordered staffing corrective action plan records, if any
Reports to the governing body

policies.title: Corporate Compliance, Fraud and Billing Integrity
policies.applies_to: Governing body, administrator, business office/billing staff, admissions staff and any employee who handles resident charges, payments or payer documents
policies.purpose: To ensure that [AGENCY NAME] bills accurately and honestly, charges only what the admission agreement and applicable payer rules allow, and handles Medicaid managed care and Optional State Supplementation (OSS) funds with integrity.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] bills and collects only for services actually provided and only in the amounts agreed in the resident contract or the applicable payer agreement. Medicaid assisted living services are paid through Statewide Medicaid Managed Care (SMMC) Long-Term Care (LTC) plans. The facility and each plan negotiate rates, and there is no state rate table (s. 409.982, F.S.). For residents who receive OSS, the facility receives the OSS base provider rate ($991.40 per month, effective June 24, 2025) and the resident keeps a personal needs allowance of $160 per month (Rule 65A-2.036, F.A.C.). The Department of Children and Families (DCF) determines OSS eligibility. The facility does not charge residents for items or services already covered by the contract rate. The OSS Alternate Care Certification form (CF-ES 1006) is kept in the record of each OSS resident, and if it cannot be obtained, the facility documents its good-faith effort to obtain it. The facility identifies state-funded residents to AHCA and DCF on request. Employees may report suspected fraud or billing errors without retaliation.

definitions.definition: A managed care plan under the Statewide Medicaid Managed Care Long-Term Care program that contracts with the facility and pays for covered assisted living services at negotiated rates.
Optional State Supplementation, a state cash assistance program for eligible residents of assisted living facilities, with eligibility determined by DCF.
The amount an OSS resident keeps for personal use ($160 per month as of June 24, 2025).
The Alternate Care Certification form kept in the record of each OSS resident.
Knowingly billing for services not provided, falsifying records to obtain payment, or charging in violation of contract or payer rules.

procedures: The governing body adopts this policy and designates the administrator as compliance officer, unless another person is named in writing.

Before billing, the business office verifies each resident's payer source and the agreed rate, and records them in the resident's financial record. For SMMC LTC residents, the rate is taken from the written agreement between the facility and the resident's plan.
The administrator ensures that the admission agreement lists the rate and each additional charge, and that no charge is made for an item or service already included in the contract rate (see RR-04).

For each OSS resident, admissions staff confirm DCF eligibility and obtain Alternate Care Certification form CF-ES 1006 and file it in the resident record. If the form is not received, staff document each request, the date and the person contacted.

For OSS residents, the business office bills the OSS base provider rate and ensures the resident receives the $160 personal needs allowance each month. The payment is documented in the resident's account (see RR-05).
Billing staff prepare invoices and claims only from documented services and census records. A second person reviews monthly invoices and plan claims for accuracy before they are sent.
Billing staff must not alter, backdate or falsify any record, signature or invoice. Any correction is made with a dated note identifying who made it and why.

Billing errors found, including overcharges and overpayments, are reported to the administrator within 5 business days, corrected, and refunded or repaid promptly with a written explanation to the resident, representative or payer.
The business office keeps a log of every overpayment, refund or credit, with amounts and dates.
When AHCA or DCF asks the facility to identify state-funded residents, the administrator provides the list by the date requested and keeps a copy of what was sent.

The administrator conducts a compliance review of billing at least every 6 months, sampling resident accounts against agreements, payer rates and service records, and reports findings to the governing body.

Employees may report suspected fraud, billing errors or improper charges to the administrator, or to the governing body if the concern involves the administrator, without fear of retaliation. The facility documents each report, investigates within 14 days and documents the outcome.
Staff training on billing integrity and this policy occurs at hire and annually (see STF-04).
Any suspected criminal billing activity is referred by the governing body to legal counsel and to the appropriate state authority.

responsibilities.duty: Adopts the policy, appoints the compliance officer, reviews semiannual compliance reports and ensures no retaliation.
Oversees billing accuracy, investigates reports, directs refunds and corrections, and responds to payer and state requests.
Verify rates and payer sources, bill accurately, keep records and report errors.
Obtain and file payer documents, including CF-ES 1006 for OSS residents.
Report suspected billing errors or fraud.

documentation: Resident financial records showing payer source and agreed rate
SMMC LTC plan rate agreements
CF-ES 1006 in each OSS resident record, or documentation of good-faith efforts to obtain it
OSS and personal needs allowance payment records
Invoices, claims and second-reviewer sign-off
Overpayment, refund and credit log
Semiannual compliance review reports
Reports of suspected fraud and investigation outcomes
Lists of state-funded residents provided on request

policies.title: Fiscal Standards, Liability Insurance and Surety Bond
policies.applies_to: Governing body, administrator, business office staff and any employee who handles resident funds or insurance documents
policies.purpose: To ensure [AGENCY NAME] keeps resident money separate from facility money, carries required liability insurance and any required surety bond, and keeps the proof of each on file.
policies.policy: Resident funds are kept separate from facility funds and are never co-mingled. A single trust account may be used if a separate written accounting is kept for each resident (Rule 59A-36.013(2)). Liability insurance is in force at all times, and proof is filed with AHCA at each renewal and each policy change (Rule 59A-36.013(4); s. 429.275(3), F.S.). The insurance certificate shows the facility name, street address, ALF type, licensed capacity and coverage dates. The rule sets no dollar minimum, so the governing body sets coverage limits with its insurance advisor. If the facility acts as representative payee for a resident or holds a power of attorney, it obtains and maintains a surety bond equal to twice the average monthly aggregate resident income received, or per resident under a power of attorney (s. 429.27(2), F.S.; Rule 59A-36.013(3)). A copy of the bond and the current insurance policy are kept on file at the facility (Rule 59A-36.015(1)). The facility also carries workers' compensation insurance as required by Florida law when it has 4 or more employees.

definitions.definition: Money belonging to residents that the facility holds for safekeeping or manages for them.
Mixing resident funds with facility operating funds, which is not allowed.
A person or entity appointed by a benefit-paying agency to receive and manage a beneficiary's benefits.
A bond that guarantees repayment of resident funds if the facility mismanages them when acting as representative payee or under a power of attorney.
Insurance covering the facility's liability for injury or loss to residents and others.

procedures: Before opening, the governing body obtains liability insurance that covers the facility name, street address, ALF type and licensed capacity, and confirms that the certificate shows the coverage dates.
The administrator keeps a copy of the current policy and certificate in the facility's records and sets a calendar reminder at least 60 days before expiration.
At each license renewal and at each policy change, the administrator submits proof of liability insurance to AHCA and keeps a copy of the submission. There must be no gap in coverage.
If a policy is cancelled, non-renewed or lapses, the administrator notifies the governing body the same day and arranges replacement coverage immediately.
The governing body confirms with its insurance advisor that workers' compensation coverage is in place if the facility has 4 or more employees, and the policy is kept on file.

The business office opens a resident trust account separate from the facility operating account. If one trust account is used for multiple residents, the business office keeps a separate written ledger for each resident.

Staff record every deposit and withdrawal on the resident's ledger on the same day, with the date, amount, purpose and the signature of the staff member and of the resident or representative where possible (see RR-05).
The business office reconciles the trust account to the total of the resident ledgers monthly. The administrator reviews and initials the reconciliation.

If the facility holds up to $500 in cash and $500 in personal effects for a resident by mutual consent, the business office documents the consent in writing and gives the resident or representative a verified statement at least every 3 months (s. 429.27, F.S.).

Before the facility agrees to act as representative payee or to accept a power of attorney for any resident, the administrator notifies the governing body, who obtains the surety bond. The facility does not take on either role until the bond is in effect.

To set the bond amount, the business office calculates twice the average monthly aggregate resident income received by the facility as representative payee. For a power of attorney, the bond is set per resident. The calculation is recalculated at each bond renewal and when residents are added or removed.
The administrator keeps a copy of the bond in effect on file and tracks its expiration date.
The administrator reports any suspected loss or misuse of resident funds to the governing body immediately and follows SAF-01 on exploitation reporting.
The governing body reviews the facility's financial statements, insurance and bond status at least annually and documents the review.

responsibilities.duty: Obtains and maintains insurance and any required surety bond and ensures adequate funding.
Files insurance proof with AHCA, keeps policies and bonds on file, and reviews trust account reconciliations.
Maintain separate resident ledgers, deposit and disburse funds, reconcile monthly and prepare quarterly statements.
Never use resident funds for facility purposes and report concerns immediately.

documentation: Current liability insurance policy and certificate
Proof of insurance filed with AHCA at each renewal and policy change
Workers' compensation policy, if applicable
Surety bond copy and bond amount calculation, if applicable
Resident trust account statements and individual resident ledgers
Monthly reconciliations with administrator initials
Written consent and verified quarterly statements for resident cash and personal effects held in safekeeping

policies.title: Resident Rights and Responsibilities
policies.applies_to: All residents and their representatives; all employees, volunteers and contracted staff
policies.purpose: To make sure every resident of [AGENCY NAME] is told of, and able to exercise, the rights in the Florida Resident Bill of Rights, and understands the house rules and resident responsibilities that apply in the facility.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will post the Resident Bill of Rights (s. 429.28, F.S.) or the Ombudsman summary of those rights in full view in a freely accessible resident area, and will include it in the admission package (Rule 59A-36.007(5)(a), F.A.C.). Written house rules in the admission package will address, at a minimum: resident responsibilities; alcohol and tobacco use; medication storage; elopement; reporting abuse, neglect and exploitation; administrative and housekeeping schedules; infection control and standard precautions; third-party providers; assistive devices; and physical restraints (Rule 59A-36.007(5)(d)). No resident will be required to work without compensation. A resident may be required to clean his or her own sleeping area only if the house rules or the resident contract say so, and any resident who is also an employee will be paid under state and federal wage law (Rule 59A-36.007(5)(e)). Residents will have convenient access to a telephone, and unidentified calls will be allowed. If the facility has a capacity of 17 or more residents and residents lack private phones, a readily accessible phone will be available on each floor of each resident building (Rule 59A-36.007(5)(f)). The facility will not require residents to use a particular health care provider (Rule 59A-36.007(3)(c)). For residents funded through a Medicaid HCBS waiver or Long-Term Care plan, the facility will also honor the federal HCBS settings requirements at 42 CFR 441.301(c)(4). That rule does not apply to residents who do not receive Medicaid HCBS or LTC funding, but all residents receive the rights described here.

definitions.definition: The statement of resident rights in s. 429.28, F.S., that must be posted and given to residents.
The written facility rules that are part of the admission package and cover the topics required by Rule 59A-36.007(5)(d), F.A.C.
A legal guardian, health care surrogate, attorney-in-fact or other person lawfully authorized to act for the resident.
Federal requirements at 42 CFR 441.301(c)(4) for home and community-based settings, which apply to residents funded through Medicaid HCBS waiver or LTC plans.

procedures: The Administrator ([ADMINISTRATOR NAME]) will post the Resident Bill of Rights, or the Ombudsman summary of rights, in full view in a freely accessible resident common area, such as the main lobby or dining room, before the facility admits its first resident.
The Administrator or designee will check the posting weekly to confirm it is still displayed, legible and unobstructed, and will record the check on the environmental rounds log.

The Administrator will maintain written house rules that cover every topic required by Rule 59A-36.007(5)(d). The Administrator will review the rules against that list at each annual policy review (see GOV-03).
The admission staff member will give the resident or representative a copy of the Bill of Rights and the house rules in the admission package before or at admission (see ADM-01 and RR-04).

The admission staff member will go over the Bill of Rights and house rules with the resident or representative in plain language and will answer questions. If the resident or representative needs language assistance or an accommodation, staff will follow RR-08.
The resident or representative will sign and date an acknowledgment that the Bill of Rights and house rules were received and explained. The signed acknowledgment goes in the resident record.

Staff will not require a resident to perform work for the facility without pay. Staff will not ask or expect residents to do laundry, kitchen, cleaning, maintenance or care tasks for the facility or other residents.

A resident may be asked to clean his or her own sleeping area only if the house rules or the contract say so. The Administrator will make sure the contract and house rules are consistent on this point.

If a resident is also employed by the facility, the Administrator will confirm that the resident is paid at or above the minimum wage required under state and federal law. The employment arrangement and pay records go in the personnel file (see STF-06).

The Administrator will make sure a telephone is readily accessible to residents at all times, including in the evening. Staff will allow unidentified calls to residents and will not screen calls or ask callers to identify themselves as a condition of passing the call on.
If the facility's capacity is 17 or more and residents do not have private phones, the Administrator will install and maintain a readily accessible telephone on each floor of each resident building.

Staff will tell residents and representatives that they may choose their own physician, pharmacy and other health care providers. Staff will arrange or help arrange care with the provider the resident chooses and will never require the use of a particular provider. Staff will document these arrangements in the care record (see ADM-03).

For residents funded through Medicaid HCBS or an LTC plan, the Administrator will review the person-centered service plan and the resident's daily routine with the plan care coordinator. The review will confirm that the resident's choice, privacy, dignity and access to the community are respected. The Administrator will document any modification of a right with the resident's consent in the service plan.
Staff will report any suspected violation of a resident right to the Administrator immediately. Complaints are handled under RR-02. Suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation is reported under SAF-01.
The Administrator will cover resident rights in new employee orientation and in annual in-service training and will keep the sign-in sheets (see STF-04).
The Administrator will review resident rights concerns, including grievances and survey findings, during quality assurance meetings (see GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Posts and maintains the Bill of Rights and house rules, makes sure no resident is required to work without pay, ensures telephone access, and trains staff on resident rights.
Delivers and explains the Bill of Rights and house rules at or before admission and obtains the signed acknowledgment.
Respect resident rights in daily care and report any suspected violation to the Administrator right away.
Follow the house rules, respect the rights of others and raise concerns through the grievance procedure.

documentation: Signed and dated resident acknowledgment of the Bill of Rights and house rules (resident record)
Current house rules with revision dates
Environmental rounds log showing weekly posting checks
Employee training sign-in sheets covering resident rights
Wage and pay records for any resident-employee
HCBS service plan review notes for Medicaid-funded residents

policies.title: Grievances and Complaints
policies.applies_to: All residents, representatives, families and facility staff
policies.purpose: To give residents and their representatives a clear way to raise complaints and recommend policy changes without fear of reprisal, and to make sure each complaint receives a timely, documented response.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains a written grievance procedure for receiving and responding to resident complaints, and a written procedure for residents to recommend changes to facility policies. The facility will be able to show that the procedure was applied whenever a complaint was received (Rule 59A-36.007(5)(b), F.A.C.; Rule 59A-36.015(1)(i), F.A.C.). The facility will post complaint numbers in full view of a common area near a resident-accessible telephone, in at least 14-point type: Long-Term Care Ombudsman 1-888-831-0404; Disability Rights Florida 1-800-342-0823; AHCA Consumer Hotline 1-888-419-3456; and Florida Abuse Hotline 1-800-962-2873 (1-800-96-ABUSE) (Rule 59A-36.007(5)(c)). Residents may use the Resident Bill of Rights grievance and facility-procedure rights in s. 429.28, F.S. The facility will show resident participation in activity planning through resident meetings, a council, a suggestion box or a similar method (Rule 59A-36.007(2)(b)). No resident will be retaliated against, discharged or threatened for making a complaint.

definitions.definition: Any complaint, oral or written, made by or for a resident about care, services, staff, other residents, the environment or facility policy.
A resident's suggestion to change a facility policy, house rule, schedule, menu or activity.
Any adverse action taken against a resident or representative because a complaint or grievance was made.

procedures: The Administrator ([ADMINISTRATOR NAME]) will post the four complaint numbers listed in this policy, in at least 14-point type, in full view of a common area near a telephone residents can use. The Administrator will check monthly that the posting is current and legible.

Staff will tell each resident and representative about the grievance procedure, the recommendation procedure and the posted hotline numbers during admission. The procedure is also included in the admission package (see RR-04).
Any employee who receives a complaint, oral or written, will accept it respectfully and will report it to the Administrator or the Administrator's designee by the end of the shift.

The Administrator or designee will record the complaint on the Grievance Log the same day, noting the date, the resident, the person making the complaint, the nature of the complaint and who received it.

Residents may make complaints orally, in writing, through a family member or representative, through the suggestion box, at a resident meeting, or directly to an outside agency. Staff will help any resident who needs help writing a complaint.
If the complaint involves suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation, the Administrator will follow SAF-01 and report to the Florida Abuse Hotline immediately. The complaint is also logged here.
The Administrator or designee will acknowledge the complaint with the resident or representative within two business days.
The Administrator will investigate by talking to the resident and involved staff, reviewing relevant records, and taking any steps needed to protect the resident while the matter is reviewed.

The Administrator will give the resident or representative a written or verbal response, with the facility's findings and any corrective action, within 14 calendar days. If more time is needed, the Administrator will explain why and give an expected date.

If the resident is not satisfied, the Administrator will remind the resident of the right to contact the Long-Term Care Ombudsman, Disability Rights Florida, the AHCA Consumer Hotline or the Abuse Hotline, and will give the resident any help needed to make the call (see RR-03).
The Administrator will record the outcome, the date of response and any corrective action on the Grievance Log and keep any related investigation notes with it.

Residents may recommend policy changes in writing, at resident meetings, through the suggestion box or directly to the Administrator. The Administrator will respond to each recommendation and record the response and any decision.
The Activities Director will hold resident meetings, or support a resident council, at least monthly. Minutes will show that residents took part in planning activities (see DL-02).
Staff will not retaliate against any resident or representative for a complaint. Any suspected retaliation will be reported to the Administrator and investigated as a grievance.
The Administrator will review the Grievance Log at least quarterly for patterns, and will present trends at quality assurance meetings (see GOV-04).
Grievance records will be kept readily available at the facility's physical address for AHCA inspection (see ADM-03 and GOV-02).

responsibilities.duty: Maintains the grievance and recommendation procedures, posts hotline numbers, investigates and answers complaints, and prevents retaliation.
Accept complaints courteously, report them to the Administrator by end of shift and never discourage or retaliate against a resident for complaining.
Holds resident meetings or supports a resident council and keeps minutes that show resident input into activities.
May raise complaints and recommend changes using any available method, including outside agencies.

documentation: Written grievance procedure and written policy recommendation procedure
Grievance Log with dates, nature of complaint, findings and outcome
Investigation notes and written responses to residents
Photograph or record of the posted hotline numbers and monthly posting checks
Resident meeting minutes or council records, and suggestion box review records

policies.title: Ombudsman Access
policies.applies_to: All residents, representatives, and facility staff
policies.purpose: To make sure residents know about the Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program and can contact an ombudsman freely, and to make sure ombudsman representatives and surveyors have the access to residents and records that the rules provide.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will give each resident or representative a Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program brochure showing the district office telephone number and address before or at admission (Rule 59A-36.006(3)(b)4, F.A.C.). The Ombudsman number, 1-888-831-0404, will be posted with the other complaint numbers in at least 14-point type (Rule 59A-36.007(5)(c), F.A.C.). The Ombudsman summary of rights may be displayed in place of the full Bill of Rights (Rule 59A-36.007(5)(a)). Access to residents and records by surveyors and ombudsman representatives is governed by Rule 59A-36.015(4), F.A.C. and the applicable statute, and the facility will cooperate fully. Residents may contact the ombudsman at any time, and staff will not discourage, screen or retaliate against a resident for doing so.

definitions.definition: The state program whose volunteers and staff advocate for residents of long-term care facilities and receive and resolve resident complaints.
The local Ombudsman Program office serving the county where the facility is located, whose address and phone number are printed on the brochure.

procedures: Before opening, the Administrator ([ADMINISTRATOR NAME]) will obtain a supply of Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program brochures for the facility's district and will confirm that the district office telephone number and address are shown.
The Administrator will restock brochures whenever supplies run low and will check at least quarterly that they are current.
The admission staff member will place a brochure in each admission package and will hand it to the resident or representative before or at admission.

The admission staff member will explain that the Ombudsman is an independent advocate, that contact is free, and that residents may call or write at any time. The staff member will record in the admission checklist that the brochure was given.

The Administrator will post the Ombudsman number, 1-888-831-0404, in at least 14-point type with the other complaint numbers, in full view of a common area near a resident-accessible telephone (see RR-02).
The Administrator will post either the full Resident Bill of Rights or the Ombudsman summary of rights in a freely accessible resident area (see RR-01).
Staff will help any resident who asks to call, write or meet with the ombudsman, including finding the number, dialing, or arranging a private space for the call.
Staff will not listen in on, screen or discourage a resident's communication with the ombudsman, and will not retaliate against a resident for contacting the ombudsman.

When an ombudsman representative arrives, the staff member on duty will greet the representative, notify the Administrator or designee, and allow access to residents. The representative may speak with any resident who is willing, and residents may choose to speak in private.

The Administrator will make the records that the rules require the facility to keep available to an ombudsman representative or surveyor as provided in Rule 59A-36.015(4). The Administrator will not release a resident's record beyond what the rules and the resident's authorization allow (see RR-07).
If the ombudsman makes a complaint or recommendation, the Administrator will respond promptly, record the matter on the Grievance Log and follow RR-02.
The Administrator will train staff on ombudsman access during orientation and at annual in-service training (see STF-04).

responsibilities.duty: Obtains brochures, maintains postings, trains staff, arranges access for ombudsman representatives and surveyors, and responds to ombudsman concerns.
Gives the brochure to each resident or representative before or at admission and documents it.
Help residents contact the ombudsman on request, and welcome ombudsman representatives without obstruction or retaliation.

documentation: Admission checklist showing the Ombudsman brochure was provided
Record of the posted Ombudsman number and Bill of Rights or summary
Grievance Log entries for ombudsman complaints and responses
Staff training sign-in sheets on ombudsman access

policies.title: Admission Agreement, Fees, Deposits and Refunds
policies.applies_to: Administrator, admission staff, business office staff, residents and representatives
policies.purpose: To make sure every resident or representative receives a written contract with all required terms before or at admission, and that fees, rate increases, deposits, refunds and bed holds are handled fairly and in writing.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will offer a contract for execution to each resident or legal representative before or at admission, and will give the resident a copy (Rule 59A-36.018(1)-(2), F.A.C.). The contract will include at least: services, supplies and accommodations; the daily, weekly or monthly rate; additional services and charges, or an attached fee schedule; at least 30 days' written notice before any rate increase; the purpose of any advance or deposit payment and a refund policy that conforms to s. 429.24(3), F.S.; a written bed hold policy; religious affiliation; written notice of the need to transfer if the resident's needs exceed the license; an assessment on admission and at least every 3 years; medication and over-the-counter medication policies; and the DNRO policy (Rule 59A-36.018(1)(a)-(m)). Additional charges require an advance itemized written statement and a signed, dated addendum (Rule 59A-36.018(3)). The facility will keep the admission package, less the contract, on file (Rule 59A-36.015(1)(g)), and will keep contracts for 5 years (Rule 59A-36.015(3)(q)).

definitions.definition: The written agreement between the facility and the resident or legal representative that contains the provisions required by Rule 59A-36.018 and s. 429.24, F.S.
Money paid by or for the resident before or at admission, whose purpose and refund terms must be stated in the contract.
Holding a resident's bed during an absence, under the facility's written bed hold policy.
A signed and dated written change to the contract that adds services or charges, supported by an itemized statement.

procedures: The Administrator ([ADMINISTRATOR NAME]) will prepare the standard resident contract and fee schedule so that it contains each provision required by Rule 59A-36.018(1)(a)-(m) and s. 429.24, F.S. The Administrator will review it against the rule at each annual policy review (see GOV-03).

Before admission, the admission staff member will give the resident or representative the contract, the fee schedule and the rest of the admission package, including the house rules, the Bill of Rights, the Ombudsman brochure, the advance directive materials and the facility's medication and DNRO policies (see RR-01, RR-03, RR-06 and HCS-01).

The admission staff member will go through each section of the contract with the resident or representative in plain language, with language assistance if needed (see RR-08). The staff member will cover the rates, what is and is not included, additional charges, deposit and refund terms, bed hold, religious affiliation, rate increase notice and transfer notice.

The contract must state the daily, weekly or monthly rate and the services, supplies and accommodations the rate covers. Any additional services and charges will be listed in the contract or in an attached fee schedule.

If the facility collects an advance or deposit, the contract will state its purpose and a refund policy that conforms to s. 429.24(3), F.S. The business office will issue a written receipt for every payment.

The contract will include the facility's written bed hold policy. Under it, the contracted rate may be charged until the facility receives written notice of a change in the resident's status, unless the resident's medical condition prevents notice and there is no responsible party.

The contract will tell the resident that the facility will give written notice of the need to transfer if the resident's needs exceed the license, and will state that an assessment is done on admission and at least every 3 years (see ADM-02 and ADM-05).

The resident or representative will sign and date the contract. The staff member will give the resident or representative a complete copy at that time and record on the admission checklist that a copy was given.

The facility will not require a resident to waive a right in the Bill of Rights as a condition of the contract, and will not require execution of a DNRO or any advance directive as a condition of admission (see RR-06).

To raise a rate, the Administrator will give the resident or representative at least 30 days' written notice before the increase takes effect. A copy of the notice goes in the resident's business file.

To add services or charges outside the contract, the Administrator will prepare an advance itemized written statement and an addendum. The resident or representative must sign and date the addendum before the new charges begin.

When a resident leaves, the business office will calculate any refund under the contract and s. 429.24(3), F.S., prepare an itemized final statement, and issue any refund due as stated in the contract.
The admission package, less the contract, will be kept on file. The signed contract will be kept for 5 years. Both will be readily available at the facility's physical address.

The Administrator will review a sample of new contracts monthly to check that each is complete, signed and dated, and that addenda are in place for additional charges. Findings go to quality assurance (see GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Maintains the contract and fee schedule, approves rate increases and addenda, and audits contracts for completeness.
Delivers and explains the contract, collects signatures and provides a copy to the resident.
Receives and receipts payments, calculates refunds, issues rate increase notices and keeps financial records of charges.
Review the contract, ask questions, and sign and date it before or at admission.

documentation: Signed and dated resident contract with a note that a copy was given (retained 5 years)
Admission package contents and checklist (kept on file, less the contract)
Fee schedule and dated written 30-day rate increase notices
Itemized statements and signed, dated addenda for additional charges
Payment receipts and final refund statements
Monthly contract audit records

policies.title: Resident Funds and Personal Property
policies.applies_to: Administrator, business office staff, all employees who handle resident money or property
policies.purpose: To protect residents' money and belongings, to keep resident funds separate from facility funds, and to make sure statements, records and any required bond are in place.
