If the facility shelters people above its licensed capacity during a declared state of emergency, the Administrator first confirms life safety is not jeopardized and needs can be met. The overage is reported to the AHCA Field Office within 48 hours, or to AHCA Central Office at (850) 412-4304.
The Administrator keeps a log of sheltered persons with name, usual address and arrival and departure dates.
After each activation and each drill, the Administrator holds an after-action review, updates the CEMP as needed and reports findings under GOV-04.

responsibilities.duty: Writes, submits, updates and keeps the CEMP, trains staff, activates and directs response, makes all reports to the county and AHCA, and stays reachable.
Carry out assigned CEMP duties, supervise staff and track residents during an emergency.
Know and carry out their CEMP duties and follow chain of command.
Provides funds and approval for emergency supplies, transport agreements and equipment.

documentation: CEMP on AHCA Form 3180-5006 (Sept 2023)
Documentation of county emergency management approval and annual submission
Significant modification submission records
Staff training records, including within 30 days of hire
Food and water supply or approved water plan records
Resident roster and evacuation tracking forms
Evacuation reports to the county and AHCA with date and time
Emergency shelter log and 48-hour report
After-action review notes

policies.title: Emergency Environmental Control (96-Hour Alternate Power)
policies.applies_to: All licensed ALF buildings, residents, and staff, including administrator, maintenance, nursing, and direct care staff, and contracted equipment vendors
policies.purpose: To keep residents safe from heat injury and other harm if primary power is lost, by maintaining a detailed Emergency Environmental Control plan that holds the building at or below 81°F for at least 96 hours. The plan supplements the Comprehensive Emergency Management Plan (CEMP) in SAF-05.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains and implements a written Emergency Environmental Control plan under Rule 59A-36.025, F.A.C. The plan provides for holding ambient temperature at or below 81°F for at least 96 hours after loss of primary power in the designated area(s). The designated area(s) provide at least 20 net square feet per resident, calculated on 80 percent of licensed bed capacity. The plan is submitted before licensure and implemented before the license is issued. Required fuel is kept onsite. The equipment is under a maintenance and testing contract. A working carbon monoxide alarm is maintained. Residents and their legal representatives are notified in writing within 5 business days of initial submission and of final implementation. Written heat-injury mitigation procedures are followed whenever power is lost. The Administrator, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME], is responsible for this policy.

definitions.definition: The portion(s) of the building where the plan holds the temperature at or below 81°F during a power loss. Together they must give at least 20 net square feet per resident.
Usable floor area of the designated area(s) available to residents, measured and recorded in the plan.
The resident count used to size the designated area(s). Example: for a licensed capacity of 40 beds, 32 residents x 20 net sq ft = 640 net sq ft minimum.
The generator or other alternate power source and the fuel supply needed to run the cooling plan. Piped natural gas qualifies as fuel.
Dehydration, heat exhaustion, heat stroke, or other harm caused by high ambient temperature.

procedures: Before licensure, the Administrator drafts the Emergency Environmental Control plan as a detailed supplement to the CEMP (SAF-05). The plan identifies the designated area(s), the cooling method, the alternate power source, and the fuel supply.

The Administrator and maintenance lead measure each designated area and record net square feet. They confirm the total is at least 20 net sq ft x 80% of licensed beds. The calculation is kept with the plan.
The plan shows how the temperature in the designated area(s) will be held at or below 81°F for at least 96 hours after power loss.
The Administrator determines the minimum onsite fuel: 48 hours of operation if licensed capacity is 16 beds or fewer, or 72 hours if 17 beds or more. Piped natural gas qualifies.

When a state of emergency is declared that may affect power at the facility, the Administrator secures fuel for 96 hours. Portable containers may be used for the portion beyond the minimum onsite supply. The fuel order and delivery are logged.

If local rules limit fuel storage, the plan states the maximum fuel stored onsite. It also names a reliable method of obtaining more fuel at least 24 hours before the supply runs out, with the vendor's name and [PHONE].
The Administrator signs a written contract with a qualified vendor to maintain and test the equipment. The contract is kept on file. Maintenance and test dates are recorded in the equipment log.
The maintenance lead installs and maintains a carbon monoxide alarm. The alarm is tested [FREQUENCY] and each test is documented.

The Administrator submits the plan to the county emergency management agency and the AHCA Assisted Living Unit before licensure. The plan is implemented, with equipment and fuel in place, before the license is issued.

Within 30 days of county approval, the Administrator emails proof of approval and a consumer-friendly summary of the plan to assistedliving@ahca.myflorida.com. A copy of the email and attachments is kept in the compliance file.

Within 5 business days of initial submission, and again within 5 business days of final implementation, the Administrator notifies each resident and legal representative in writing. Dated copies of the notices and a distribution list are kept.

Each year the plan is reviewed and resubmitted as required. Residents and representatives are notified again only if the plan is significantly modified. Any significant modification is submitted and notified within the same 5-business-day timeframe.

The written heat-injury mitigation procedures cover four areas. First, cooling devices, including their location, number, and placement for use. Second, ice and refrigeration for medications that require refrigeration, coordinated with HCS-01. Third, staff wellness checks of residents for dehydration and heat injury, at the frequency written in the plan. Fourth, medical intervention for any resident in jeopardy, including calling the physician or 911 and transfer under HCS-04.

When power is lost, the person in charge activates the plan, notifies the Administrator, moves residents to the designated area(s) as needed, and starts wellness checks. Each check is documented with time, resident name, findings, and staff initials.
After any power loss or activation, the Administrator reviews performance with staff within [NUMBER] days and records corrections in the QAPI file (GOV-04).
All staff are trained on the plan at orientation and annually, and the training is documented (STF-04).

responsibilities.duty: Develops, submits, implements, and annually reviews the plan. Secures fuel, holds vendor contracts, sends the AHCA email, and issues resident notices.
Measures space, maintains and tests equipment and the carbon monoxide alarm, and logs fuel and tests.

responsibilities.role: Person in charge / direct care staff
responsibilities.duty: Activate the plan during power loss, perform and document wellness checks, and implement the heat-injury procedures.
Protect refrigerated medications and notify the provider when a resident is at risk.

documentation: Emergency Environmental Control plan and net square foot calculation
County approval and copy of the email to AHCA with the consumer-friendly summary
Resident and representative notices and distribution lists
Equipment maintenance and testing contract and logs
Fuel supply records, fuel vendor information, and fuel order logs
Carbon monoxide alarm test log
Wellness check records and post-event reviews
Staff training records

policies.title: Fire Safety, Evacuation and Drills
policies.applies_to: All buildings, residents, staff, and contractors; Administrator, maintenance, and direct care staff
policies.purpose: To protect residents from fire by maintaining a building that meets the Florida Building Code and ch. 69A-40 fire standards, by passing the annual fire inspection, and by making sure staff know the facility's evacuation procedures.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] complies with the Florida Building Code and the Uniform Fire Safety Standards in ch. 69A-40, F.A.C. The local fire authority or State Fire Marshal inspects fire safety (Rule 59A-36.005, F.A.C.). The Administrator sends each annual fire inspection report to the AHCA Central Office within 30 calendar days (Rule 59A-36.004, F.A.C.) and keeps each report for 2 years (Rule 59A-36.015, F.A.C.). Corrections are made promptly. The Administrator knows that AHCA may require additional staff if the fire authority reports that the facility fails fire safety standards, until the authority confirms compliance (Rule 59A-36.010, F.A.C.). The facility considers its ability to meet ch. 69A-40 requirements for each resident when making admission decisions. All staff are trained in emergency procedures, chain of command, and evacuation roles within 30 days of hire.

definitions.definition: The local fire department or fire marshal, or the State Fire Marshal where applicable, that inspects the facility under ch. 69A-40.
The written order of who is in charge and directs evacuation when the Administrator is not present.
A staff member's assigned duties during an alarm or evacuation, such as assisting specific residents, checking rooms, or meeting at the assembly point.
A practice of the alarm and evacuation response, conducted at the frequency and in the manner required by the local fire authority and ch. 69A-40.

procedures: The Administrator schedules the annual fire inspection with the local fire authority or State Fire Marshal. The inspection date is calendared as a standing item.
After each inspection, the Administrator receives the written report and records the date it was received.
The Administrator sends a copy of each annual fire inspection report to the AHCA Central Office within 30 calendar days. Proof of sending is kept with the report.
The Administrator keeps fire inspection reports on file at [ADDRESS] for at least 2 years. They are available to AHCA surveyors on request.
Cited deficiencies are corrected promptly. The Administrator records the correction, the date, who completed it, and any re-inspection or written confirmation from the fire authority.

If the fire authority reports that the facility fails fire safety standards, the Administrator immediately reviews staffing (STF-01). The Administrator complies with any AHCA order for additional staff until the fire authority confirms compliance.

Before any building is placed under the license or any space is converted to resident use, the Administrator confirms it has been inspected. Uninspected space is not used by residents until the required prior AHCA approval is obtained (GOV-02).

The Administrator obtains the drill frequency, alarm, and sprinkler requirements that apply to this facility in writing from the local fire authority and ch. 69A-40. These are entered in the Fire Safety Schedule: [FIRE DRILL FREQUENCY AND DRILL TIMES PER LOCAL FIRE AUTHORITY].
The Administrator conducts drills on the schedule in the Fire Safety Schedule. Drills are conducted on all shifts and include the evacuation routes. Staff in the chain of command direct the drill.
After each drill, the Administrator or designee records date, time, shift, participants, time to complete, problems found, and corrective actions.
The Administrator posts evacuation routes and the written chain of command. Evacuation roles are assigned on each shift's written schedule.
The maintenance lead checks that exits, alarms, extinguishers, and detectors work and are unobstructed, as the fire authority requires. Findings are logged and repaired promptly.
Within 30 days of hire, each new staff member is trained in the facility's emergency procedures, including chain of command and their evacuation role (STF-04). The training is signed and dated.

During pre-admission screening, the admitting staff member considers whether the facility can meet ch. 69A-40 requirements for that resident, including the ability to evacuate with the staff available (ADM-01, ADM-04). The conclusion is documented in the screening.
All physical plant work and renovations comply with the Florida Building Code and ch. 69A-40. The Administrator keeps permits and approvals on file.
The Administrator reports fire safety findings and drill results to the QAPI committee (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Schedules inspections, sends reports to AHCA within 30 days, keeps reports 2 years, corrects deficiencies, obtains drill requirements, and ensures training.
Maintains and checks fire safety systems and exits, logs repairs, and supports inspections.
Directs evacuation per the chain of command and ensures staff perform assigned roles.
Know evacuation routes and their assigned roles, take part in drills, and report hazards.

documentation: Annual fire inspection reports (kept 2 years) and proof of submission to AHCA Central Office
Deficiency correction log and re-inspection confirmations
Written drill requirements from the local fire authority and the Fire Safety Schedule
Fire drill records
Chain of command and evacuation role assignments
Staff emergency procedure training records
Permits and approvals for building changes
Admission screening notes addressing ability to meet fire safety standards

policies.title: Infection Prevention and Control
policies.applies_to: All staff, contracted staff, and volunteers who provide personal services, handle medications, or have resident contact; residents; Administrator and nursing staff
policies.purpose: To prevent the spread of infection among residents, staff, and visitors through hand hygiene, standard precautions, equipment disinfection, admission screening, staff exclusion, and training.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains an infection prevention and control program under Rule 59A-36.007, F.A.C. Staff perform hand hygiene before and after personal services when exposure to infectious materials or body fluids is expected, using alcohol rub, antiseptic wash, or soap and water. Staff follow standard precautions, using gloves, gown, mask, and eye protection or face shield according to the exposure. Reusable medical equipment and communal assistive devices are cleaned and disinfected before and after each use, following manufacturer recommendations. Admission screening excludes residents with a communicable disease likely to be transmitted to others. The medical exam addresses TB, MRSA, scabies, and other communicable disease. Staff with a known or suspected communicable disease are removed from duty until a provider's statement shows there is no risk. Staff receive infection control training before providing personal care. The county health department inspects sanitation and biomedical waste.

definitions.definition: Infection control practices applied to all residents regardless of diagnosis, including hand hygiene and use of protective equipment based on expected exposure.
Cleaning hands with alcohol-based rub, antiseptic wash, or soap and water.
Equipment used by more than one resident, such as a shared walker, wheelchair, lift, or blood pressure cuff.
An illness that can be transmitted to other persons, including TB, MRSA, and scabies.
Gloves, gowns, masks, eye protection, and face shields.

procedures: The Administrator designates an infection control lead, [NAME/TITLE], who monitors practices and reports to the Administrator.

Staff perform hand hygiene before and after personal services whenever exposure to infectious materials or body fluids is expected. They use alcohol rub, antiseptic wash, or soap and water as appropriate. Alcohol rub dispensers and handwashing supplies are kept stocked in care areas.

Staff apply standard precautions with every resident. They select gloves, gown, mask, eye protection, or face shield according to the anticipated exposure. PPE is stocked at [LOCATION] and replaced after use.

Staff clean and disinfect reusable medical equipment and communal assistive devices before and after each use. They follow the manufacturer's recommendations for cleaning agents and contact times. The cleaning is recorded on the [EQUIPMENT CLEANING LOG].
During pre-admission screening (ADM-01), the admitting staff member reviews the resident's health information for communicable disease likely to be transmitted. Such residents are not admitted.
The Administrator confirms the medical examination form addresses TB, MRSA, scabies, and other communicable disease before admission is finalized. Incomplete forms are returned to the provider.

Staff report to the Administrator or person in charge any known or suspected communicable disease in themselves. The Administrator removes the employee from duty until a provider's written statement shows the employee presents no risk. The statement is placed in the personnel record (STF-05, STF-06).

Before providing personal care, new staff receive 1 hour of infection control training, including universal precautions and facility sanitation, using these facility policies. Nurses, CNAs, and home health aides are exempt from this requirement. A completed 29 CFR 1910.1030 bloodborne pathogens training record satisfies the requirement. The training is documented (STF-04).
Staff trained in assistance with medications follow infection control procedures when assisting with medications (HCS-02). This includes hand hygiene and clean handling of devices.

Staff handle sharps, contaminated materials, and biomedical waste according to the facility's exposure control practices and the requirements of the county health department. Staff report exposure incidents to the Administrator immediately.

Staff use the Incident and Accident process (SAF-02) to report outbreaks. The Administrator notifies the physician, the county health department, and others as required, and isolates or separates affected residents as ordered.
The infection control lead reviews infection events and compliance quarterly and reports to the QAPI committee (GOV-04).
The Administrator keeps county health department sanitation and biomedical waste inspection results on file and corrects any findings promptly.

responsibilities.duty: Oversees the program, excludes ill staff, ensures training and admission screening, and responds to inspection findings.
Monitors hand hygiene, PPE supplies, and equipment cleaning, and tracks infections.
Follow hand hygiene and standard precautions, disinfect equipment, and report symptoms.
Follow cleaning and waste handling procedures (DL-03).

documentation: Infection control training records, including any 29 CFR 1910.1030 records
Equipment cleaning logs
Admission screening and medical exam forms addressing communicable disease
Staff exclusion notices and return-to-work provider statements
Infection and outbreak logs and reports
County health department inspection reports
QAPI infection control review minutes

policies.title: Smoking, Alcohol, Visitors and Pets
policies.applies_to: Residents, visitors, staff, and volunteers
policies.purpose: To state clear house rules on smoking, alcohol, visitors, and animals that protect resident safety and respect resident rights, privacy, and freedom of choice.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] includes house rules on alcohol and tobacco use in the admission package given to each resident (Rule 59A-36.007, F.A.C.). The facility keeps a written visitation policy as a required facility record (Rule 59A-36.015, F.A.C.). Residents' privacy and telephone access rights are respected at all times. The facility's pet policy, which is an operator choice, is stated in the house rules. Where service animals are allowed, the facility addresses its ADA obligations and infection control practices. Smoking is allowed only where the house rules permit it and where state law and local ordinance permit it. House rules are applied consistently and never used to limit rights otherwise protected by law.

definitions.definition: Written facility rules given to residents in the admission package, including rules on alcohol and tobacco.
The written policy stating when and how visitors may see residents.
An animal trained to perform tasks for a resident with a disability. The facility's ADA obligations apply.
A companion animal kept by a resident or the facility that is not a service animal, as permitted by the facility's pet policy.

procedures: The Administrator writes the house rules, including rules on alcohol and tobacco use, and reviews them annually (GOV-03). The rules state where, if anywhere, smoking is permitted. Any smoking area must comply with state law and local ordinance and be outdoors or otherwise as the law permits.

The Administrator writes the visitation policy. It states visiting hours or the absence of limits, how visitors check in, and any limits needed for resident safety or infection control. The policy is kept as a required facility record at [ADDRESS].
The Administrator also ensures a copy of the visitation policy is available for inclusion with the AHCA license application or renewal, where required.

At or before admission, the admitting staff member gives the resident and any representative the house rules (including alcohol and tobacco) and the visitation policy. The resident or representative signs an acknowledgment (RR-04).
Residents are not asked to waive rights because of the house rules. Rules are applied equally to all residents (RR-01, RR-08).
Staff allow residents to receive visitors in privacy, subject only to the visitation policy and the resident's wishes. A resident may refuse any visitor.
Staff ensure residents have access to a telephone and reasonable privacy for calls (RR-01).

Alcohol: staff follow the house rules and the resident's care plan and physician orders. If a resident's alcohol use may interact with medications or create a safety concern, staff notify the physician and record it in the resident record.

Smoking: staff supervise smoking safety as the care plan requires. Smoking materials and lighters are kept as the house rules direct. Staff check that smoking is permitted only in the designated area.

Pets and service animals: the Administrator decides, based on the pet policy, whether a resident's animal is allowed. For a service animal, the Administrator discusses the request with the resident and follows ADA requirements, including permitted inquiries. The Administrator also sets infection control expectations (SAF-08), such as hand hygiene after animal contact and keeping animals out of food preparation areas.

Residents who keep animals are responsible for their care, as stated in the pet policy. If an animal creates a safety or health problem, the Administrator documents it and works with the resident on a solution before any action is taken.
Staff report any visitor conduct that threatens resident safety to the Administrator, who may restrict that visitor and documents the decision. Suspected abuse by a visitor is reported under SAF-01.
Violations of house rules are addressed by the Administrator with the resident, documented, and handled through the grievance process when the resident objects (RR-02).
The Administrator reviews complaints and incidents involving smoking, alcohol, visitors, or animals during QAPI review (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Writes and reviews the house rules, visitation policy, and pet policy, and decides requests regarding animals and visitor restrictions.
Give house rules and visitation policy at or before admission and obtain acknowledgment.
Apply rules fairly, supervise smoking safety, protect resident privacy, and report problems.

documentation: Current house rules, including alcohol and tobacco rules
Written visitation policy
Signed resident acknowledgments of house rules and visitation policy
Pet and service animal decisions and related notes
Visitor restriction decisions and reasons
Grievance and incident records related to these rules

policies.title: CPR, First Aid and Automated External Defibrillator
policies.applies_to: All staff on all shifts; Administrator; staff scheduling; maintenance
policies.purpose: To make sure someone trained in CPR and First Aid is always in the facility, and that the AED required for facilities of 17 or more beds is available and working.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] keeps at least one staff member with current First Aid and CPR cards in the facility at all times (Rules 59A-36.010 and 59A-36.011, F.A.C.). CPR certification must include an in-person skills demonstration and be issued by an instructor or provider approved by the American Red Cross, American Heart Association, National Safety Council, or an organization accredited by the Commission on Accreditation for Pre-Hospital Continuing Education. A nurse is considered to hold First Aid. An EMT or paramedic certified under Florida law is considered to hold both First Aid and CPR. If licensed for 17 or more beds, the facility keeps a working AED on the premises at all times (s. 429.255, F.S.). Staff honor a valid DH Form 1896 (Do Not Resuscitate Order) when presented.

definitions.definition: A hands-on practice and testing of CPR technique observed by an instructor. Online-only courses do not qualify.
Automated External Defibrillator, a device that analyzes heart rhythm and delivers a shock if needed.
The Florida Do Not Resuscitate Order form, which staff must honor when valid (see RR-06).

procedures: The Administrator keeps a roster of all staff showing First Aid and CPR card issuer and expiration dates. A copy of each card is kept in the personnel record (STF-06).

Before approving CPR training for staff, the Administrator verifies the course requires an in-person skills demonstration and that the instructor or provider is approved by the American Red Cross, American Heart Association, National Safety Council, or an organization accredited by the Commission on Accreditation for Pre-Hospital Continuing Education.

The Administrator or scheduler builds the written 24-hour schedule (STF-01) so that at least one staff member with current First Aid and CPR is in the facility on every shift, including nights, weekends, and holidays. The Administrator reviews the schedule weekly.
A nurse on duty counts as holding First Aid, but still needs a current CPR card to meet the CPR requirement. An EMT or paramedic certified under Florida law counts for both.

If a scheduled trained staff member calls out and no other trained staff member is available, the person in charge notifies the Administrator immediately. The Administrator arranges a trained replacement before the shift starts.
The Administrator tracks expiration dates monthly and enrolls staff in renewal courses at least 60 days before cards expire. No staff member is counted as the trained person after the card expires.
At orientation, new staff are told which staff on each shift are CPR and First Aid trained, and where the first-aid kit and AED are located (STF-04).
If the facility is licensed for 17 or more beds, the Administrator places a working AED in an accessible, marked location. All staff are shown where it is during orientation.

The maintenance lead checks the AED [FREQUENCY], including battery and pad expiration dates, and records the check in the AED log. Defective or expired parts are replaced immediately. If the AED is out of service, the Administrator notifies staff and arranges a replacement as soon as possible.

In a medical emergency, staff call 911, begin First Aid or CPR as appropriate, and use the AED if indicated. Before starting CPR, staff check the resident's record for a valid DH Form 1896 (RR-06). If a valid DNRO is presented, staff do not begin resuscitation and follow HCS-09.
The person in charge notifies the Administrator, physician, and legal representative as soon as the emergency permits, and documents the event under SAF-02 and HCS-04.
After each emergency, the Administrator reviews the response with staff, restocks supplies, and checks the AED. Findings are given to the QAPI committee (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Ensures a trained person is on every shift, verifies course providers, tracks expirations, and provides the AED where required.
Staffs each shift with a CPR and First Aid trained person and notifies the Administrator if none is available.
Keep cards current and respond to emergencies, including using the AED.
Checks and logs the AED and first-aid supplies.

documentation: CPR and First Aid roster and copies of cards
Course provider approval verification
Written 24-hour staffing schedules showing the trained person on each shift
AED location record and inspection log (17+ beds)
Emergency response and incident reports
Orientation records showing staff were told of the AED and first-aid supplies

policies.title: Food Service and Therapeutic Diets
policies.applies_to: Administrator, food service designee, kitchen and dining staff, contracted food vendors, and nursing and direct care staff who serve or assist with meals
policies.purpose: To provide nutritious, safe, and appropriately timed meals and snacks that follow dietary guidelines and provider orders, and to keep required food service records.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] provides food service under Rule 59A-36.012, F.A.C. The Administrator or a written designee is responsible for total food service and day-to-day supervision of food staff. Meals follow the USDA Dietary Guidelines for Americans 2020-2025 and the Dietary Reference Intakes (2019). Menus are reviewed annually by a dietitian, nutritionist, or supervised registered dietetic technician, dated, planned at least 1 week ahead, and kept as served for 6 months. Therapeutic diets are provided as ordered by the provider. Meal timing limits are observed. A 3-day supply of nonperishable food is kept. County health department inspection reports are kept for 2 years.

definitions.definition: The person named in writing by the Administrator to be responsible for total food service and day-to-day supervision of food staff.
A diet ordered by the resident's provider for a medical condition, such as diabetic, low sodium, or texture-modified diets.
A tested written recipe giving ingredients, amounts, preparation steps, and yield. Required except when the facility has 16 or fewer residents.
The menu actually served, with any substitutions noted.
Registered dietetic technician.

procedures: The Administrator is responsible for total food service or names a food service designee in writing. The designation is dated and filed in the compliance records.

A designee who has not completed the core training course must complete the core course's food and nutrition module before assuming responsibility. Exempt are a certified food manager, certified dietary manager, registered or licensed dietitian, dietetic registered technician, or health department sanitarian. Proof is kept with the designation.

The Administrator or designee completes 2 hours of continuing education in nutrition and food service each year. Staff who prepare or serve food and have not taken the core training complete 1 hour of safe food handling within 30 days of hire. Both are documented (STF-04).

The designee plans meals using the USDA Dietary Guidelines for Americans 2020-2025 and the Dietary Reference Intakes (2019). Standardized recipes are used unless the facility has 16 or fewer residents.

A dietitian, nutritionist, or supervised RDT reviews all regular and therapeutic menus at least annually. The reviewer signs and dates the menus and records their license or registration number. Menus show portion sizes.
Menus are dated and planned at least 1 week ahead. They are posted or easily available to residents.
Kitchen staff note substitutions on the menu as served. Menus as served are kept for 6 months at [ADDRESS].

The nurse or designee records each resident's therapeutic diet order from the provider in the resident record and communicates it to the kitchen on a diet list. Staff serve therapeutic diets exactly as ordered (ADM-03).
If a resident refuses a therapeutic diet, staff document the refusal and notify the provider. Staff also notify the resident's representative when appropriate (RR-01).

The designee schedules meals so that no more than 14 hours pass between the evening protein meal and the morning meal, and 2 to 6 hours pass between meals. A snack is offered at least daily to residents without kitchen access.

The designee keeps a 3-day supply of nonperishable food, based on current census, and a water supply or written water plan as the rule requires. The supply list is reviewed [FREQUENCY] and with the emergency plan (SAF-05). Stock is rotated and dated.
Kitchen staff follow safe food handling and sanitation practices. Staff who handle food practice hand hygiene (SAF-08).
The Administrator keeps county health department inspection reports for 2 years. If the facility is required to be inspected, the Administrator keeps current reports and corrects findings promptly.

If food service is contracted, the Administrator keeps the written contract and the contractor's licenses on file. The contractor's menus and diets must meet these standards, and the Administrator remains responsible for compliance.
The Administrator reviews resident food complaints and weight concerns, and reports trends to the QAPI committee (GOV-04). Resident complaints are handled under RR-02.

responsibilities.duty: Is responsible for total food service or designates a qualified designee in writing, and keeps records and contracts.
Plans and supervises menus, diets, supplies, and kitchen staff and ensures training.
Reviews, signs, and dates menus annually.
Transmit diet orders, serve therapeutic diets correctly, and document refusals and provider notification.
Prepare and serve meals as written and handle food safely.

documentation: Written food service designee appointment and qualifications
Training records (nutrition and food service CE, safe food handling)
Dated menus with portion sizes and signed annual dietitian review with license/registration number
Menus as served with substitutions (kept 6 months)
Standardized recipes (if more than 16 residents)
Therapeutic diet orders, diet list, and refusal documentation
3-day nonperishable food supply list and water plan
County health department inspection reports (kept 2 years)
Contracted food service agreements and contractor licenses

policies.title: Activities and Social Programming
policies.applies_to: All residents; Activities Coordinator, Administrator, direct care staff
policies.purpose: To make sure every resident has access to a diversified, ongoing activities program that fits their needs, abilities and interests. The program must meet the Florida minimum schedule and be planned with resident input.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] provides an ongoing activities program of individual and group activities suited to each resident's needs, abilities and interests, as required by Rule 59A-36.007(2), F.A.C. Scheduled activities are offered at least 6 days a week and for at least 12 hours per week. Television does not count toward the 12 hours unless it is a special one-time event of interest to residents. Time residents spend in an outside day program may be counted. The monthly activities calendar is posted in the common areas. Residents are consulted on the selection, planning and scheduling of activities, and the facility keeps evidence of that consultation. Participation is voluntary, and each resident's choice to participate or decline is respected.

definitions.definition: A planned individual or group activity that appears on the posted calendar and is led or supported by staff or a volunteer. Routine television viewing is not a scheduled activity.
A televised event of particular interest to residents (for example, a major sporting event or ceremony) that may be counted toward the weekly hours on that occasion only.
A special activity that residents help plan. Up to 3 hours may be credited toward the weekly minimum.
A documented way of consulting residents, such as meetings, committees, a resident council, a monitored suggestion box, group discussions or questionnaires.

procedures: The Administrator designates an Activities Coordinator in writing, or assumes the duties personally, and records the designation in the facility's administrative file.

Within 30 days of admission, and again at each reassessment, the Activities Coordinator or designee records each resident's interests, abilities, cognitive and physical limitations, cultural and religious preferences, and past hobbies. This is done through a resident or representative interview and is documented in the resident's record.

The Activities Coordinator builds a monthly calendar that schedules activities on at least 6 days of every week and totals at least 12 hours per week. The calendar mixes group and individual activities, including ones for residents with limited mobility, cognitive impairment or hearing and vision loss.

The Activities Coordinator excludes routine television from the weekly hour count. A special one-time television event may be counted only if it is marked on the calendar as a special event of interest to residents.
If residents attend an outside day program, the Activities Coordinator may count those hours. The coordinator documents the attendance and hours.

If residents help plan a special activity, the Activities Coordinator records the planning (date, participants, what they planned). Up to 3 hours may then be credited toward the weekly minimum. The coordinator does not credit more than 3 hours.

The Activities Coordinator posts the current calendar in the common areas at a height and size residents can read, by the 25th of the prior month or before the month starts. Large print or verbal reminders are provided on request. Copies are available to residents and representatives on request.

The facility maintains at least one resident input mechanism (resident council, meetings, committee, monitored suggestion box, group discussion or questionnaire). Resident input is gathered at least quarterly, and the Activities Coordinator reviews the results.

The Activities Coordinator records the date, topic, attendees and resulting calendar changes each time residents are consulted. Suggestion boxes are emptied and reviewed at least weekly and responses are documented.

Direct care staff invite and encourage residents to take part and provide assistance (transport within the building, setup, cueing). Staff do not coerce participation. A resident's refusal is respected and noted.

For residents who do not or cannot join group activities, staff offer individual activities such as one-to-one visits, music, reading, sensory activities or hobbies. Individual activities are documented.
Activity supplies and equipment are kept clean and in working order. Outings and activities that involve risk follow the Transportation (DL-04) and Falls Prevention (HCS-06) policies.
The Activities Coordinator keeps a daily attendance or participation record. At month end the coordinator totals scheduled hours by week and gives the totals to the Administrator.
The Administrator reviews the monthly totals. If any week falls below 6 days or 12 hours, the Administrator documents the reason and the corrective step taken.
The Administrator presents activity program results and resident feedback in the Quality Assurance review (GOV-04) at least quarterly.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures the program meets the 6-day, 12-hour minimum, designates and supports the Activities Coordinator, reviews monthly totals and takes corrective action.
Assesses interests, builds and posts the calendar, leads or arranges activities, runs resident input processes, and keeps attendance and hour records.
Encourage and assist residents to participate, support individual activities and report resident preferences to the Activities Coordinator.
May take part in planning, give suggestions, and choose whether to participate.

documentation: Monthly activities calendars with posting dates
Daily attendance or participation logs
Weekly and monthly hour totals reviewed by the Administrator
Resident interest and ability assessment entries in the resident record
Resident council, committee or meeting minutes, questionnaires and suggestion box logs
Records of resident-planned special activities and credited hours
Documentation of outside day program attendance if counted

policies.title: Housekeeping, Laundry and Maintenance
policies.applies_to: All residents; Administrator, Maintenance, Housekeeping and Laundry staff
policies.purpose: To keep the facility clean, safe, sanitary and in good repair, to provide resident furnishings, linens and laundry service as promised, and to make sure physical plant changes do not violate licensure requirements.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains the building, grounds and equipment in a clean, safe and sanitary condition under the Florida Building Code and fire standards referenced in Rule 59A-36.014, F.A.C. Where the facility furnishes the bedroom, it provides a bed with a mattress at least 36 x 72 inches, closet or wardrobe space, a dresser, a nightstand or table, a lamp and a wastebasket, plus a chair on request. The facility provides linens and laundry service. The facility keeps master keys to resident bedrooms. House rules state the administrative and housekeeping schedules and requirements. Residents may be required to clean their own sleeping areas only if the house rules or resident contract say so. Any maintenance or construction that would change licensed capacity or convert uninspected space to resident use must have prior AHCA approval under Rule 59A-36.004, F.A.C. Emergency power equipment is maintained and tested under a maintenance contract.

definitions.definition: A key held by the facility that opens resident bedrooms so staff can enter in an emergency or to provide care.
Any area that has not been inspected and approved for resident use under the facility's license (for example, a garage, storage area or newly built wing).
The written rules given to residents that state the facility's administrative and housekeeping schedules and requirements.
Scheduled inspection, servicing and testing of building systems and equipment to prevent failure.

procedures: At or before admission, the Administrator or designee gives the resident the house rules, including housekeeping and administrative schedules. The resident or representative signs for receipt, and the signed copy goes in the resident record.

Before move-in, Housekeeping staff verify that each bedroom provided by the facility has a bed and mattress at least 36 x 72 inches, closet or wardrobe space, a dresser, a nightstand or table, a lamp and a wastebasket. A chair is added on request. The checklist is signed and dated.

Housekeeping staff clean common areas, bathrooms and kitchen areas daily according to the posted housekeeping schedule. They use facility-approved disinfectants and follow the Infection Prevention and Control (SAF-08) policy.

Housekeeping or direct care staff clean resident rooms on the schedule stated in the house rules. Residents are required to clean their own sleeping areas only if the house rules or resident contract say so. Staff do not require a resident to do so otherwise.

Laundry staff launder facility linens and resident personal laundry at least weekly, and sooner when soiled. Soiled and clean items are kept separate, and soiled linen is handled with standard precautions. Laundry service is provided as stated in the contract.
Laundry staff label resident clothing, and report lost or damaged items to the Administrator the same day. Loss reports are handled under Resident Funds and Personal Property (RR-05).

The Administrator keeps master keys to resident bedrooms in a secure location. Staff access to master keys is limited to those on duty who need them. Staff knock and respect resident privacy before entering, except in an emergency.

The Maintenance Lead inspects the building, grounds, handrails, floors, lighting, water temperature, call or alert systems and exits at least monthly using a written checklist. Hazards are corrected promptly. Hazards that cannot be fixed immediately are reported to the Administrator and made safe.
Staff report any repair need to the Maintenance Lead the same shift using the work order log. The Maintenance Lead records the date, problem, action taken and completion date.

The Administrator keeps a written contract with a qualified vendor to maintain and test emergency power equipment. Test results are kept in the maintenance file and reviewed by the Administrator. See SAF-06.

Before any renovation, addition, change in room use, or change in the number of licensed beds, the Administrator contacts AHCA. If the change would alter capacity, the Administrator obtains prior AHCA Central Office approval. If the change would convert uninspected space to resident use, the Administrator obtains prior AHCA Field Office approval. The Administrator documents the approval before work or resident use begins.

The Administrator confirms that all buildings operated under the one license are on contiguous property and that the facility does not offer or represent services beyond those authorized by its license.
The Administrator sends copies of the annual fire inspection and sanitation inspection to the AHCA Central Office within 30 calendar days of receipt, and keeps the transmittal proof on file.
The Administrator reviews housekeeping, laundry and maintenance findings, complaints and work order trends at least quarterly in the Quality Assurance process (GOV-04).
Staff who handle chemicals use them according to the label and Safety Data Sheets, and store them away from resident-accessible areas, medications and food.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures furnishings, linens, laundry and maintenance meet this policy, keeps master keys secured, obtains AHCA approvals before capacity or space changes, and sends inspection copies to AHCA within 30 days.
Performs monthly inspections, completes work orders, and manages vendor contracts including emergency power testing.
Clean, launder and report hazards and missing or damaged items according to the posted schedule.
Report maintenance, safety and housekeeping needs and respect resident privacy and property.

documentation: House rules with signed resident receipt
Room furnishing checklists
Housekeeping and laundry schedules and completion logs
Monthly maintenance inspection checklists and work order log
Emergency power maintenance contract and test records
Master key control log
AHCA approval letters for capacity changes or conversions
Fire and sanitation inspection reports and proof of transmittal to AHCA within 30 calendar days

policies.title: Transportation
policies.applies_to: All residents; Administrator, designated staff and drivers
policies.purpose: To make sure residents can get to the medical, dental, nursing and mental health services they need, to be clear in advance about the availability and cost of transportation, and to protect resident safety and independence.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] provides transportation to needed medical, dental, nursing or mental health services, or arranges it through family, friends, volunteers, taxis, public buses or agencies, as required by Rule 59A-36.007(3), F.A.C. Staff assist residents in making and remembering appointments. The admission package states the availability and cost of transportation. Any charge beyond the contract rate requires an itemized statement and a signed, dated addendum as required by Rule 59A-36.018, F.A.C. Evacuation transportation is addressed in the facility's Comprehensive Emergency Management Plan. Residents who are able may travel independently in the community.

definitions.definition: Transportation the facility schedules through a third party such as family, friends, volunteers, taxis, public buses or agencies when the facility does not drive the resident itself.
A written, signed and dated amendment to the resident contract that adds services or charges, supported by an itemized statement.
A resident's travel in the community without staff, consistent with the resident's assessment, care plan and resident rights.

procedures: During pre-admission screening and the admission process, the Administrator or designee asks each resident and representative about transportation needs, ability to travel independently, mobility devices and usual providers.

The admission package states in writing whether the facility provides transportation, which trips are covered, and the cost of each type of trip. The Administrator reviews this section with the resident or representative and obtains a signature acknowledging receipt.

If the facility charges for transportation beyond the contract rate, the Administrator prepares an itemized statement of the charge and a contract addendum. The resident or representative signs and dates the addendum before the charge begins. Copies are given to the resident and filed in the record.

When a resident has a medical, dental, nursing or mental health appointment, staff record it on the resident's appointment calendar and on the master appointment log, including date, time, provider, address, purpose and who will provide transportation.
Staff remind the resident and the representative of upcoming appointments at least 1 day in advance, or more often if the resident has memory impairment.

The Administrator or designee arranges transportation at least 2 business days ahead whenever possible. If the facility cannot provide the ride, staff arrange it through family, friends, volunteers, taxis, public buses or agencies, and record who is providing it.
If the resident needs wheelchair-accessible or other special transportation, staff confirm accessibility with the provider when booking.

Before the trip, staff give the escort or driver the resident's face sheet, current medication list, questions or concerns from staff, and any physician orders or forms, as needed. Staff protect the resident's privacy under RR-07.

A trained staff member, family member or other escort accompanies a resident who needs assistance, who has cognitive impairment or elopement risk (see SAF-03 and HCS-05), or whose care plan requires it.

Staff drivers hold a valid Florida driver license. The facility confirms and files a copy. Facility vehicles are kept insured, inspected and maintained, and used only according to the facility's written vehicle procedures. Wheelchair securement and seat belts are used for every trip.

If a resident wishes to travel independently in the community, the Administrator or Nurse reviews the resident's most recent assessment and care plan. Staff ask the resident to tell staff when leaving and returning. The resident's choice is respected. Any safety concerns are discussed with the resident and representative and documented.
After a trip, staff or the escort report any change in condition, new orders or follow-up appointments. Staff update the resident record and notify the representative as needed under HCS-04.
If a trip is missed or cancelled, staff reschedule it the same day and notify the provider and the resident. The reason is recorded in the appointment log.
Transportation for evacuation follows the transportation arrangements in the Comprehensive Emergency Management Plan (SAF-05). The Administrator reviews those arrangements at least annually.
The Administrator reviews missed appointments, transportation complaints and costs at least quarterly in the Quality Assurance process (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Ensures transportation is provided or arranged, that availability and cost are stated in the admission package, that charges follow the addendum process, and that vehicles and drivers are in compliance.
Maintains the appointment calendar, books and confirms rides, reminds residents and communicates with providers and families.
Transport safely, use securement and seat belts, accompany residents who need help, and report changes in condition.
Share transportation needs, confirm appointments, and tell staff when traveling independently.

documentation: Admission package transportation disclosure with signed acknowledgment
Itemized statements and signed contract addenda for transportation charges
Master appointment log and resident appointment calendars
Driver license copies and vehicle insurance and maintenance records
Post-trip notes, changes in condition and follow-up appointments in the resident record
Records of missed or rescheduled appointments

policies.title: Staffing Levels and Supervision
policies.applies_to: All staff; Administrator, Managers and scheduling personnel
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] always has enough qualified staff on duty to meet residents' scheduled and unscheduled needs, the Florida minimum staff hours, and the supervision requirements for every shift.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] meets or exceeds the minimum weekly staff hours in Rule 59A-36.010(3), F.A.C., based on the combined number of residents, day care participants and respite residents. At least one staff member with access to facility and resident records is in the facility at all times when residents are present. At 17 or more residents, at least one staff member is awake at all hours. The facility keeps a written 24-hour work schedule. Staffing is always sufficient to meet resident needs, resident contracts and the care standards, regardless of the minimum. The facility complies immediately with any AHCA order for additional staff. Staff are paid at least the Florida minimum wage, which is $15.00 per hour from September 30, 2026.

definitions.definition: The minimum total direct staff hours per week by resident count: 0-5 residents = 168; 6-15 = 212; 16-25 = 253; 26-35 = 294; 36-45 = 335; 46-55 = 375; 56-65 = 416; 66-75 = 457; 76-85 = 498; 86-95 = 539; plus 42 hours for every 20 residents over 95.
Each resident, day care participant and respite resident receiving services. Independent living residents who receive no personal, LNS or ECC services are not counted.
A staff member who is awake and on duty, not sleeping, throughout the overnight hours. Required at 17 or more residents.

Hours worked by on-the-job staff providing resident care or supervision. Maintenance, grounds, clerical and food-preparation-only staff are not counted. The administrator or manager counts only if actively involved in day-to-day operation and on the staffing schedule.

procedures: Each Monday, or on the first business day of each week, the Administrator or designee counts the current residents, day care participants and respite residents. Independent living residents who receive no personal, LNS or ECC services are excluded from the count.
The Administrator finds the minimum weekly staff hours for that census from the table in this policy and records the required total on the staffing worksheet.

The scheduler prepares a written work schedule that shows the 24-hour staffing pattern, listing each staff member's name, position and shift for every day. The schedule is posted or made available to staff at least 7 days in advance.

The scheduler totals the countable hours on the schedule. Maintenance, grounds, clerical and food-preparation-only staff are excluded. The administrator or manager is included only if actively involved in day-to-day operation and shown on the schedule. Only on-the-job staff hours are counted.
If the countable hours are below the minimum, the scheduler adds shifts before the week begins and the Administrator approves the change.

The scheduler assigns at least one staff member with access to facility and resident records for every hour residents are present. No resident who is serving as paid or volunteer staff is left solely in charge.
When the facility has 17 or more residents, the scheduler assigns at least one awake staff member for every overnight hour. Awake status is confirmed by the supervisor on rounds.

The Administrator checks that staffing is enough for residents' scheduled and unscheduled needs, which includes the resident contracts, care plans, ADL needs, the memory care needs (HCS-05) and any ECC, LNS or LMH services the facility is licensed to provide. If acuity increases or call-outs occur, the Administrator adds staff even when the minimum hours are met.
For LMH, ECC and LNS licenses, the Administrator also applies the additional staffing rules for each license type and documents that they are met.

For a call-out or no-show, the supervisor follows the on-call list, offers shifts to qualified staff, or uses a contracted staffing agency under a written contract. The supervisor records the change on the schedule. A shift is never left without required coverage.

The Administrator keeps the written work schedules and time sheets for the most current 6 months. At a licensed capacity of 17 or more, the facility also keeps written job descriptions and time sheets for all staff.
The Administrator provides direct care staff schedules to residents or their representatives on request and records the request and date provided.

If AHCA requires staffing above the minimum, the Administrator provides the staff immediately, submits the corrective action plan AHCA requires by the deadline set, and documents when the added staff began.

The Administrator confirms with payroll at least annually, and when the minimum wage changes, that all staff are paid at least the Florida minimum wage ($15.00 per hour from September 30, 2026) and records the review.
The Administrator reviews staffing worksheets, call-outs and resident care concerns at least quarterly in the Quality Assurance process (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Ensures minimum hours and awake overnight staffing are met, approves schedules, responds to AHCA staffing orders and verifies minimum wage compliance.
Counts residents, prepares and totals schedules, arranges coverage and keeps schedules and time sheets.
Confirms required staff are on duty and awake as needed, and reports gaps immediately.
Report as scheduled, record accurate time and notify the supervisor promptly of absences.

documentation: Weekly census and minimum staff hour worksheets
Written work schedules showing the 24-hour staffing pattern (kept 6 months)
Time sheets (kept 6 months)
Written job descriptions (required at licensed capacity of 17 or more)
Staffing agency contracts
AHCA staffing orders, corrective action plans and proof of added staff
Requests for direct care schedules and dates provided
Annual minimum wage verification

policies.title: Administrator and Manager Qualifications and Absence Coverage
policies.applies_to: Administrator, Managers, designated in-charge staff and the governing body
policies.purpose: To make sure the person responsible for daily operation meets Florida qualifications and training requirements, and that a qualified person is always in charge when the administrator is away.
policies.policy: The Administrator of [AGENCY NAME] meets the qualifications of Rule 59A-36.010(1), F.A.C.: at least 21 years of age; a high school diploma or GED if employed on or after October 30, 1995; Level 2 background screening; and completion of the core training and competency test no later than 90 days after becoming administrator, with continuing education afterward. The facility complies with Rule 59A-36.011, F.A.C. and s. 429.52, F.S. An administrator who is absent for more than 48 hours with residents on the premises designates in writing a staff member at least 21 years old who is physically present and in charge. No staff member who is not an administrator or manager is in charge for 21 or more consecutive days or 60 total days in a calendar year.

definitions.definition: A minimum of 26 hours of required training, followed by a competency test with a 75% minimum passing score, completed within 3 months.
12 hours of CE related to assisted living every 2 years. ECC and LMH CE count toward the requirement as described in Rule 59A-36.011.
A person appointed in writing by an administrator who oversees more than one facility, to manage a specific facility.
A staff member at least 21 years old who is designated in writing and physically present when the administrator or manager is absent for more than 48 hours.

procedures: Before hiring or appointing an Administrator, the governing body or owner verifies age (at least 21), education (high school diploma or GED if employed on or after October 30, 1995), and Level 2 screening clearance. Copies are placed in the personnel file.

The governing body records the Administrator's start date as the date the person became administrator. The Administrator must complete the 26-hour core training and the competency test no later than 90 days after that date, and within 3 months of it. The Administrator's calendar of due dates is kept in the personnel file.

The Administrator schedules the competency test promptly after the core training. The passing score is 75%. The test fee may not exceed $200 per attempt. The facility records the score and the date of passing, and files the certificate.
If the Administrator is a licensed nursing home administrator, the facility keeps a copy of the license as proof of exemption from the core training and competency test.

The Administrator completes 12 hours of CE related to assisted living every 2 years. The Administrator keeps certificates and a CE tracking log. ECC and LMH CE hours are counted only as described in Rule 59A-36.011.

The governing body checks the CE log at least 90 days before each 2-year deadline. An administrator who lets CE lapse must retake the core training and competency test. The governing body will not allow a lapse.
When there is a change of administrator, the owner or new administrator notifies AHCA within 10 days on AHCA Form 3180-1006, and files proof of submission.

In extenuating circumstances such as the administrator's death, the owner contacts AHCA immediately. AHCA may allow an individual to serve temporarily for up to 90 days while completing required training. The owner documents the AHCA authorization and the individual's training progress.

If one person serves as administrator of more than one facility, the owner confirms the Administrator does not exceed 3 facilities and appoints a manager in writing for each facility. Each manager meets the same qualifications as an administrator that apply, and the written appointments are kept on file.

Before any absence expected to exceed 48 hours with residents on the premises, the Administrator or manager designates in writing a staff member who is at least 21 years old to be in charge. The designee must be physically present in the facility during the absence. The written designation includes the dates, the designee's name, and contact information for the Administrator.

The Administrator confirms the designee holds current CPR and First Aid certification or that another certified staff member is on duty, is oriented to emergency procedures, and knows how to reach the Administrator, the owner and the on-call nurse.

The Administrator tracks the days each non-administrator staff member is in charge. No such staff member is in charge for 21 or more consecutive days or 60 total days in a calendar year. If the limit would be reached, the Administrator or a manager resumes charge or the owner arranges a qualified replacement.
The Administrator keeps the written designations and the day-count log in the administrative file and makes them available to AHCA on request.
The governing body reviews the Administrator's and managers' qualification, training and absence coverage records at least annually and documents the review (GOV-01).

responsibilities.duty: Verifies qualifications, appoints managers in writing, ensures timely training and CE, notifies AHCA within 10 days of an administrator change and handles extenuating circumstances.
Completes core training, the competency test and CE on time, designates in-charge staff in writing, and tracks days in charge.
Meets the same qualification and training requirements and manages the assigned facility day to day.
Is present in the facility, at least 21 years of age, and follows emergency and notification procedures during the absence.

documentation: Administrator and manager personnel files with proof of age, education, screening and training
Core training certificate and competency test score
CE certificates and tracking log
AHCA Form 3180-1006 and proof of submission
Written manager appointments
Written in-charge designations for absences over 48 hours
Log of days in charge by non-administrator staff
AHCA authorization for temporary service, if applicable

policies.title: Background Checks and Employee Registries
policies.applies_to: Owners and controlling interests, Administrator, managers, all employees and contracted staff who provide services to residents
policies.purpose: To protect residents by making sure everyone who works in or provides services at [AGENCY NAME] has passed Florida Level 2 background screening, is rescreened on schedule and has documentation on file.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] requires Level 2 background screening for the administrator, managers and all staff, including staff contracted by the facility to provide services to residents, as required by Rule 59A-36.010, F.A.C. and ss. 408.809 and 429.174, F.S. Screening is run through the AHCA Care Provider Background Screening Clearinghouse under s. 435.12, F.S. Staff are rescreened every 5 years. The facility keeps documentation of Level 2 compliance in each personnel record, as required by Rule 59A-36.015, F.A.C. For staff supplied by a licensed staffing agency, the facility keeps a written contract that describes the services provided. Controlling interests are also screened. The facility verifies professional licenses, such as nursing licenses, and keeps copies.

definitions.definition: Fingerprint-based state and national criminal history screening under ss. 408.809 and 435.12, F.S., with results shared through the AHCA Clearinghouse.
The AHCA system through which screening results are shared among agencies and providers. Help line: 850-412-4503.
Individuals or agency personnel who provide services to residents under a contract with the facility, who are screened the same as employees.
An owner or other person with the authority to direct the facility's management or policies, who must be screened as part of licensure on AHCA Form 3110-1008 and its addendum (Form 3110-1024).

procedures: Before the first day of work, the Administrator or designee gives every new hire or contracted worker the screening instructions and explains that Level 2 screening is a condition of employment or contract.

The Administrator or designee submits the applicant's fingerprints through an approved electronic vendor, and enters the facility's information into the AHCA Clearinghouse so that results can be shared with the facility. The person does not start duties involving resident contact until the facility has received an eligible screening result in the Clearinghouse.

If the applicant was previously screened and the results are available in the Clearinghouse, the Administrator confirms eligibility and the screening is current before the person starts. The Administrator records the confirmation date and files a copy.

If the Clearinghouse shows the applicant is ineligible or has a disqualifying offense, the Administrator does not employ or contract with the person and handles any exemption process as AHCA requires. The Administrator records the decision.
The Administrator places documentation of Level 2 compliance in each employee's personnel record, including the date and result of screening and the date of the next rescreening.

For staff supplied by a licensed staffing agency, the Administrator keeps the written staffing agency contract, which describes the services provided, in place of personnel records, and confirms the agency's license and its screening responsibilities in the contract.

For each contracted individual who provides services directly to residents and is not supplied by a licensed staffing agency, the facility screens the person through the Clearinghouse and files documentation as for employees.

The Administrator maintains a rescreening tracker listing each person's screening date and the date 5 years later. The tracker is reviewed monthly. Rescreening is started at least 90 days before the due date, and results are recorded in the personnel file.

For the Administrator, managers and each controlling interest, the owner ensures screening is completed and the facility keeps documentation. Ownership and controlling interest information is reported on AHCA Form 3110-1008 and addendum Form 3110-1024, and changes are reported to AHCA as required.

The Administrator verifies the license of any nurse or other licensed professional using the Florida Department of Health license lookup before the person starts, and again at renewal. A copy of the verified license is kept in the personnel record. This policy does not adopt a separate nurse aide registry requirement for a standard ALF.

If staff are arrested or charged with a disqualifying offense, or if the facility learns of a change in eligibility, the Administrator removes the person from resident contact immediately, checks the Clearinghouse and follows AHCA direction. The action is documented.
If the facility has trouble with the Clearinghouse, the Administrator contacts the Clearinghouse help line at 850-412-4503 and records the call.

The Administrator audits all personnel and contract files at least annually to confirm that screening documentation, rescreening dates and license verifications are complete, and reports results to the governing body and in Quality Assurance (GOV-04).
Screening results and criminal history information are confidential and kept in a secure location, with access limited to the Administrator, owner and AHCA surveyors.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures screening is completed before resident contact, maintains the Clearinghouse relationship and the rescreening tracker, verifies licenses and keeps documentation.
Ensures controlling interests, the Administrator and managers are screened and that ownership information is reported to AHCA.
Gives screening instructions, submits fingerprints and files results as directed.
Complete screening honestly and promptly and report any arrest or charge to the Administrator.

documentation: Level 2 screening results and Clearinghouse eligibility confirmations in each personnel record
Rescreening tracker (5-year cycle)
Staffing agency contracts that describe services provided
Copies of professional licenses and verification dates
AHCA Form 3110-1008 and addendum 3110-1024 for controlling interests
Records of any exclusion or removal decision
Annual personnel file audit

policies.title: Hiring, Orientation and Ongoing Training
policies.applies_to: All employees, contracted and agency staff, managers and the administrator of [AGENCY NAME], including those working under the ECC, LNS and LMH specialty licenses, if any.
policies.purpose: To make sure every person who works in the facility is qualified for the job, has completed the orientation and training Florida requires before and after beginning work, and has proof of that training in the personnel record for AHCA surveyors.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] hires only staff who are qualified for their duties by education, training and experience (Rule 59A-36.010, F.A.C.). No new employee who has not completed core training may have contact with residents until he or she has completed at least 2 hours of preservice orientation and the employee and the administrator have signed the orientation statement. Staff complete the in-service training required by Rule 59A-36.011, F.A.C. within the stated deadlines. This includes infection control before personal care is given, medication assistance training before a staff member assists with medications, and elopement response training for all staff. Administrators complete the core training, competency test and continuing education required by Rule 59A-36.011, F.A.C., Rule 59A-36.010, F.A.C. and s. 429.52, F.S. First Aid/CPR, ADRD, ECC and LMH training are managed under SAF-10, HCS-05, HCS-11 and HCS-12. All required training is documented in the personnel record, which is kept at the facility and available to AHCA (Rule 59A-36.015, F.A.C.).

definitions.definition: At least 2 hours of orientation given before a new employee who has not completed core training interacts with residents. It covers resident rights and the facility's license type and services, and is acknowledged by a statement signed by the employee and the administrator.
The 26-hour core training and competency test required of administrators (75% to pass), completed within the time allowed by rule.
Employees who provide personal care, supervision or assistance with activities of daily living (ADLs) to residents.

Training given after hire on required topics: infection control, adverse incidents and emergency procedures, resident rights and abuse, neglect and exploitation, resident behavior and ADL assistance, safe food handling, elopement response and HIV/AIDS.

A 6-hour course taught by a registered nurse or pharmacist that staff must complete before assuming the duty of assisting with self-administration of medications. Two hours of continuing education are required each year.
Activities of daily living, such as bathing, dressing, eating, toileting, transferring and ambulating.

procedures: Before making a job offer, the administrator or designee reviews the position's duties and the applicant's education, training, experience, licenses and certifications and decides whether the person is qualified for the duties (Rule 59A-36.010). The administrator keeps this review with the application.

The administrator or designee tells the applicant that employment depends on completing background screening (STF-03), the health statement and TB documentation (STF-05) and the training in this policy.

On or before the first day of work the administrator or designee opens a personnel record and a Training Tracking Log for the employee, listing each required course, its due date and its completion date (see STF-06).

No new employee who has not completed core training may interact with residents until he or she has completed the 2-hour preservice orientation. The administrator or a trained designee delivers it, covering at minimum resident rights (RR-01) and the facility's license type and the services it provides, including any ECC, LNS or LMH designation.
At the end of orientation, the employee and the administrator sign and date the preservice orientation statement. The administrator places it in the personnel record the same day.
Before the employee provides any personal care, the employee receives 1 hour of infection control training (SAF-08). The trainer documents the date, content outline, length and trainer name.
Within 30 days of hire, direct care staff complete 1 hour of training on reporting adverse incidents and on emergency procedures (SAF-02, SAF-05).

Within 30 days of hire, direct care staff complete 1 hour of training on resident rights and on preventing and reporting abuse, neglect and exploitation (RR-01, SAF-01), unless the employee has completed core training.

Within 30 days of hire, direct care staff complete 3 hours of training on resident behavior and needs and on assisting with ADLs. Nurses, CNAs and home health aides are exempt from this 3-hour requirement if their license or certification applies. The administrator keeps a copy of the license or certificate in the record.
Within 30 days of hire, every employee completes the one-time HIV/AIDS course required by state law, unless a valid certificate of prior completion is on file.
All staff, regardless of position, complete elopement response training within 30 days of hire (SAF-03). The training is repeated as part of annual in-service planning.

Employees who prepare or serve food complete 1 hour of safe food handling training within 30 days of hire unless they have completed core training. Food service staff also complete the food service continuing education required by Rule 59A-36.011 (DL-01).

Before a staff member assists any resident with self-administered medication, the staff member completes the 6-hour medication assistance course taught by a registered nurse or pharmacist. The administrator verifies the certificate and does not add the person to the medication assistance schedule until it is on file. The staff member completes 2 hours of continuing education on medication assistance each year (HCS-02).

The administrator confirms that First Aid/CPR training (SAF-10), ADRD training (HCS-05) and, if the facility holds those licenses, ECC training (HCS-11) and LMH training (HCS-12) are completed within the deadlines in those policies.

The administrator completes the 26-hour core training and the competency test (75% to pass) within 90 days of becoming administrator and then 12 hours of continuing education every 2 years (Rule 59A-36.010; s. 429.52, F.S.). The governing body checks completion at each evaluation.

The administrator reviews each Training Tracking Log at least monthly. Any overdue training is reported to the employee's supervisor. The administrator may remove the employee from the affected duty until the training is complete, and documents the action taken.

When a staffing agency supplies staff, the administrator obtains proof of the training required by this policy or provides it before the person works with residents, and files the proof in the agency staff file (STF-01).
The administrator reports training completion status to the governing body and QA committee each quarter (GOV-04) and addresses gaps in the next quarter's training plan.

responsibilities.duty: Ensure all staff are qualified, delivers or arranges orientation and training, signs orientation statements, monitors due dates monthly and completes own core training and continuing education on time.
Prevent untrained staff from performing duties they are not yet trained for, report overdue training to the administrator and verify competence of staff on the floor.
Complete all required training by the due date, sign attendance and acknowledgment records and give the administrator copies of outside certificates and licenses.
Teach the 6-hour medication assistance course and the annual continuing education, and document content, length and attendees.
Review training compliance reports and ensure resources are available for required training.

documentation: Qualification review at hire
Signed and dated preservice orientation statement (employee and administrator)
Training Tracking Log for each employee
Sign-in sheets, course outlines, trainer names and certificates for each in-service topic
Medication assistance course certificate and annual continuing education records
Core training and competency test certificates and 12-hour continuing education records for the administrator
Copies of licenses and certifications (RN, LPN, CNA, HHA) used for exemptions
