Agency staff training proof
Quarterly training compliance report to governing body and QA committee

policies.title: Employee Health and TB Screening
policies.applies_to: All new and current employees, managers, the administrator and contracted staff who work at [AGENCY NAME].
policies.purpose: To protect residents and staff from communicable disease by making sure every staff member has a health care provider's statement and current TB documentation on file, and that anyone with a communicable disease is removed from duties until cleared.
policies.policy: Within 30 days of hire, each new staff member submits a written statement from a health care provider that the person has no signs or symptoms of communicable disease. The examination must have been done no earlier than 6 months before the statement is submitted. Each staff member also has documentation of a negative tuberculosis examination every year. Staff who have, or are suspected of having, a communicable disease are removed immediately from duties until a written provider statement shows they pose no risk. All documentation is kept in the personnel record at the facility (Rule 59A-36.010 and Rule 59A-36.015, F.A.C.). Occupational bloodborne pathogen protections are applied as required by OSHA.

definitions.definition: A written statement from a licensed health care provider that the staff member has no signs or symptoms of communicable disease.
A person newly hired. A staff member who transfers without a break in service between facilities under the same ownership or management is not new for this requirement.
An illness that can be spread from person to person that could put residents or staff at risk.

Documentation of a negative tuberculosis examination every year. A statement from the Department of Health or a provider of a TB testing material shortage satisfies the annual requirement for that period.

procedures: At the time of the job offer, the administrator or designee gives the applicant a written notice of the health statement and annual TB requirements and a form the health care provider can use for the statement.
The administrator or designee records the hire date and the due date (30 days after hire) for the health statement in the employee's Training and Compliance Log (see STF-06).

The administrator or designee checks that each health statement submitted is signed and dated by a health care provider, states the person has no signs or symptoms of communicable disease and is based on an exam done no earlier than 6 months before the date the statement is submitted.

If the statement does not meet these standards, the administrator returns it to the employee the same day with a written request for a corrected statement and notes the due date. The 30-day deadline is not extended.

For a staff member transferring from another facility under the same ownership or management without a break in service, the administrator confirms the transfer date, obtains a copy of the existing health statement and TB record and files it, so a new statement is not required.

The administrator or designee ensures that each staff member has documentation of a negative TB examination within the past year. The tracking log shows the next due date, and the administrator or designee sends a written reminder to staff at least 30 days before it.

If the Department of Health or the provider of a TB testing material announces a testing material shortage, the administrator files the written shortage statement in each affected employee's record. It stands in for the annual test for that period, and the administrator schedules testing as soon as the shortage ends.

If an employee has a positive TB test, the administrator obtains a written provider statement that the person is not a risk to others before the person works with residents, and files it in the record.

If a staff member reports, or a supervisor observes, signs or symptoms of a communicable disease (for example fever with cough, diarrhea or vomiting, rash or skin lesions that could spread infection), the supervisor removes the person from duty immediately and notifies the administrator.
The administrator documents the date and time of removal, the symptoms reported and the actions taken in a confidential employee health entry that is separate from resident records.
The employee may not return to duty until the administrator has a written provider statement showing the person is not a risk to residents or staff. The statement is filed in the personnel record.
The administrator reports any suspected outbreak among residents or staff as directed in SAF-08 and notifies the county health department as required.

The administrator, with the QA committee, identifies employees who have occupational exposure to blood or other potentially infectious material and applies the OSHA bloodborne pathogens requirements in SAF-08, including the exposure control plan, training and the offer of hepatitis B vaccination.

For contracted and agency staff, the administrator confirms in the written staffing agency contract that the health statement and annual TB documentation are provided, and keeps copies in the agency staff file before the person works a shift.

Each month the administrator reviews the compliance log for missing or expiring health statements and TB documentation. Staff who are late are given written notice and not scheduled until the documentation is received, unless the administrator documents another compliant plan.
Employee health information is kept confidential and available only to the administrator, designee, surveyors and others permitted by law.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures health statements and annual TB documentation are obtained on time, removes ill staff from duty, tracks due dates and keeps health records confidential.
Remove from duty any staff with signs of communicable disease and notify the administrator immediately.
Obtain the provider statement and annual TB documentation by the due date and report any symptoms of communicable disease before working.
Supply the required documentation for contracted staff as required by contract.

documentation: Health care provider statement, dated no more than 6 months before submission
Annual TB documentation, including any provider or DOH shortage statements
Provider statement clearing a positive TB result
Employee health removal and return-to-duty log, with provider clearance statements
Compliance tracking log with due dates
Transfer verification for staff moving between commonly owned or managed facilities
Bloodborne pathogen exposure control plan, training and vaccination offer or declination records

policies.title: Personnel Records
policies.applies_to: The administrator, managers, all employees, and contracted and agency staff of [AGENCY NAME].
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] keeps a complete, organized and confidential personnel record for every staff member, available at the facility for AHCA review, and that wage and staffing documentation meets Florida requirements.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains a personnel record for every employee and for contracted staff. Records are kept at the facility's physical address and are readily available to AHCA during any inspection (Rule 59A-36.015, F.A.C.; s. 429.275, F.S.). Each record contains the items listed in this policy, including background screening, health and TB documentation, orientation and training, qualifications and the job description. Records of contracted staff include the written staffing agency contract (Rule 59A-36.010, F.A.C.). Pay for every employee is at or above the Florida minimum wage under Art. X, s. 24 of the Florida Constitution: $14.00 per hour from September 30, 2025 and $15.00 per hour from September 30, 2026. Personnel records are confidential and are retained for the period required by Rule 59A-36.015, F.A.C. and any longer period required by other law.

definitions.definition: The file that holds all employment, qualification, screening, health, training and performance documents for one staff member.
Persons who work in the facility under a contract or through a staffing agency rather than as direct employees.
Kept at the facility's physical address and produced to AHCA or other authorized persons promptly on request.
The hourly wage floor set by Art. X, s. 24 of the Florida Constitution, $15.00 per hour from September 30, 2026 (and $14.00 per hour from September 30, 2025).

procedures: The administrator designates a locked, fire-resistant storage location for personnel records at the facility address [ADDRESS] and names a records custodian. For electronic records, the administrator makes sure they can be printed or displayed immediately for a surveyor.
On or before the employee's first day, the records custodian creates a personnel record containing the employment application, the date of hire, the job title and a written job description.

The record includes the Level 2 background screening results and employee registry or other screening documentation as required in STF-03, with the date of screening and the eligibility determination. No one works with residents until screening is complete as set in STF-03.

The record includes the health care provider statement (within 30 days of hire) and annual TB documentation as required in STF-05. Detailed health information is kept in a separate confidential section of the file.

The record includes the signed and dated preservice orientation statement and all training records required in STF-04. These include in-service topics, infection control, HIV/AIDS, elopement, safe food handling, medication assistance and annual continuing education, plus First Aid/CPR (SAF-10), ADRD (HCS-05), ECC (HCS-11) and LMH (HCS-12) training if applicable.

The record includes proof of qualifications for the position, such as education, licenses or certifications (RN, LPN, CNA, HHA) and the administrator's core training certificate, competency test result and continuing education certificates (STF-02).
For contracted and agency staff, the custodian keeps the written contract with the staffing agency and the proof of screening, health, TB and training for each individual working in the facility.

The custodian maintains the written 24-hour staffing schedule and the weekly staff-hours records required by STF-01 and keeps time and attendance records showing who worked, which shifts and how many hours.

The custodian keeps payroll records that show each employee's hourly rate. Before each pay period closes, the administrator confirms that no employee is paid less than the current Florida minimum wage and updates rates before the effective date each time the minimum wage rises.
The custodian keeps current liability insurance information and any other records required by s. 429.275, F.S. in the business and facility files as described in GOV-06.

Each month the administrator audits a sample of personnel records, and at least once a year audits every record, using a personnel record checklist. Missing items are given a correction date no more than 14 days out. The administrator documents the audit and follow-up.

Only the administrator, the records custodian and designated management may open personnel records. Employees may see their own records on request, in the presence of the administrator or designee. Surveyors and other authorized officials are given immediate access during inspections.
Records are never removed from the facility except by copy for a lawful purpose. A sign-out log records any copy released, the date, the person receiving it and the reason.

When an employee leaves, the administrator records the separation date, reason and any exit information, and moves the file to closed storage. Closed records are kept at the facility, or at another location only if they can be produced to AHCA promptly, for the full period required by Rule 59A-36.015, F.A.C. and any longer period required by law or set by the governing body.

Records are destroyed only after the retention period has passed, with the administrator's approval, and a destruction log is kept showing what was destroyed, the date and the method (shredding or secure electronic deletion).
The administrator reports the results of personnel record audits to the governing body and QA committee each quarter (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Ensures complete personnel records are kept at the facility, conducts audits, verifies minimum wage compliance and controls access and retention.
Creates and maintains files, tracks expiring items, handles the sign-out log and prepares records for inspections.
Provide accurate information and copies of licenses, certificates and updates (for example address changes and renewals) to the administrator.
Reviews audit results and ensures sufficient resources for compliant record keeping.

documentation: Personnel record for each employee and each contracted staff member
Application, job description and proof of qualifications
Background screening results (STF-03)
Health statement and annual TB documentation (STF-05)
Orientation statement and training records (STF-04)
Staffing agency contracts
24-hour staffing schedule, timesheets and weekly staff-hour records
Payroll records showing wage rates at or above the Florida minimum wage
Personnel record audit checklists and follow-up notes
Record sign-out log and records destruction log
